Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 1:

Tafsir of Surat al-An'am

He said, may Allah be pleased with him: Know that Surat al-An'am is Meccan. Yusuf ibn Mihran narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: Surat al-An'am was revealed all at once in Mecca at night, and with it seventy thousand angels escorting it with glorification (tasbih). This has also been narrated as a marfu' report traced to the Prophet. In the complete form of the report from the Prophet, he said: "Whoever recites it in a night, the seventy thousand angels will seek forgiveness for him, those angels, night and day, until morning." In some narrations: "Those angels had a loud sound of glorification, and the earth was shaking, while the Prophet was saying: Glory be to my Lord, the Mighty, until it was revealed." In the narration of al-Kalbi from [Abu] Salih from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: Surat al-An'am was revealed all at once in Mecca except for two verses: His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Come, I will recite﴾ to the end of the verse, and His saying: ﴿They have not measured Allah with His true measure﴾ to the end of the verse. In some narrations: "except for three verses: from His saying ﴿Say: Come﴾ to the end of the three verses." It is also narrated from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Surat al-An'am is among the choice (najaib) of the Qur'an. And from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Whoever recites Surat al-An'am has attained the pleasure of his Lord.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate

﴿Praise belongs to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darknesses and the light; yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Praise belongs to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾. It is related from Ka'b al-Ahbar that he said: This verse is the first verse in the Torah, and the last verse in the Torah:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And say: Praise belongs to Allah, who has not taken a son﴾ to the end of the verse.

So His saying ﴿Praise belongs to Allah﴾ means: "Praise Allah." The statement is expressed in the form of a report but carries the meaning of a command. Its purpose is both to command praise and to teach how to praise, for if it had said "Praise Allah," there would be a need to explain the manner of praise. As for His saying ﴿who created the heavens and the earth﴾, He singled them out for mention because they are the greatest of creatures as far as the servants can see, and because in them are lessons and benefits for the servants.

﴿And made the darknesses and the light﴾. The word "ja'ala" (made) here means "khalaqa" (created). Then they differed. Some said: the darknesses are the night and the light is the day. Others said: by the darknesses He means disbelief (kufr), and by the light, faith (iman). The darknesses include all darknesses, even the darkness of the heart, the darkness of doubt, and the like. The light includes all lights, even the light of the heart, the light of certainty, and the like. It was also said: by the darknesses is meant ignorance (jahl), and by the light, knowledge ('ilm). And it was said: by the darknesses is meant disobedience (ma'siyah), and by the light, obedience (ta'ah).

It is narrated from Qatadah that he said: Allah, may He be exalted, created the heaven before the earth, the night before the day, and Paradise before the Fire. But others have said: He created the earth before the heaven, and this will come later.

﴿Yet those who disbelieve ascribe equals to their Lord﴾. Al-Kisa'i said: "adala al-shay' bi al-shay'" means to equate one thing with another when he makes it equal to it, and from it comes "al-'adl" (justice). Its meaning is: they ascribe to Allah others besides Allah as equals. Mujahid said: its meaning is: "thumma alladhina kafaru bi-rabbihim yushrikun" (then those who disbelieve in their Lord associate partners). The two meanings are close, because whoever makes something other than Allah equal to Allah has committed shirk. It was also said: His saying ﴿Yet those who disbelieve﴾ carries a subtle meaning, similar to the saying of one who says: "I bestowed on you such-and-such, and I favored you with such-and-such, then you do not thank me, then you disbelieve in my blessing."

The Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on Surah 6, verse 2:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾. This means, as we have explained, that Allah, exalted is He, commanded the Angel of Death until he took a handful of earth, and from it He created Adam, may the blessings of Allah be upon him. This is the meaning of His saying: ( ﴿It is He who created you from clay﴾ then decreed a term, and a specified term with Him). Ibn 'Abbas said: The first term is from birth to death, and the second term is from death to the Resurrection. He also said: Every person has two terms: a term until death, and a term from death to the Resurrection. If he is dutiful and keeps the ties of kinship, a portion of the term of Resurrection is added to his lifespan; and if he is otherwise, a portion of his lifespan is reduced and that portion is added to the term of Resurrection.

It was also said: The first term is the term of this world, as we have explained, and the second term is from the beginning of the Hereafter. That is specified with Allah, and no one knows it besides Him. ﴿Yet you still doubt﴾, that is, you dispute.

Allah's saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth; He knows what you conceal and what you disclose﴾. Ibn al-Anbari said: its meaning is: "He is Allah, the one worshipped in the heavens and on the earth." Others said: its construction is: "He is Allah, who knows your secret and your open affairs in the heavens and on the earth," and this is the view of al-Zajjaj. ﴿And He knows what you earn﴾. Al-kasb (earning, acquisition): every action a person performs with effort in order to bring about a benefit or ward off a harm. For this reason the act of Allah is not described as kasb, because His act is free of seeking benefits and averting harms.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 4:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And never comes to them any sign from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it.﴾ By this verse He meant the splitting of the moon (inshiqaq al-qamar). The disbelievers asked the Messenger of Allah to bring them a sign, and he (ﷺ) said: "What is it that you want?" They proposed the splitting of the moon, so he brought it to them, and they disbelieved and turned away.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So they have denied the truth when it came to them﴾, meaning: what we have mentioned. {So there will come to them the news of that at which they used to mock}. Its meaning: the consequence of that at which they used to mock will surely come back to them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 6:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have they not considered how many generations We destroyed before them?﴾ It has been said: eighty years. It has also been said: sixty years. It has also been said: forty years. It has also been said: thirty years. According to the memorizers of hadith (huffaz al-hadith), however, a qarn (generation) is one hundred years, for it is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said to 'Abd Allah ibn Busr al-Mazini: "You will live a qarn," and he lived one hundred years. They took this as evidence that a qarn is one hundred years. In the reports: between Adam and Noah there were ten qurun, and between Noah and Abraham there were ten qurun. The qarn in reality is the people of each era, whether or not a prophet was sent among them. This is indicated by his saying (ﷺ): "The best of people is my qarn, then those who follow them, then those who follow them," meaning: then the qarn who follow them.

And His saying: ﴿We had established them in the land as We have not established you﴾, meaning: We gave them what We did not give you.

﴿And We sent down the sky upon them in abundant rain﴾, meaning: continuous, one after another. The poet said:

(And may he give you drink from the star-rain of Thurayya, a stream away from the milking, a continuous heavy downpour)

That is, continuous. Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning, "And We sent down the sky upon them in abundant rain," is: continuous at times of need, and it does not mean continuous without interruption. ﴿And We made the rivers flow beneath them, then We destroyed them for their sins and produced after them another generation.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 7:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And if We had sent down to you a written scroll on paper﴾. The occasion of this was that ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Umayya al-Makhzumi, the brother of Umm Salama, said to the Messenger of Allah: "We will not believe in you until you bring down to us a book from the heaven all at once." So He sent down His saying: ﴿And if We had sent down to you a written scroll on paper﴾. Al-qirtas (paper): it is that which is written upon; if it is not written upon, it is called ṭars (a blank sheet).

﴿So they touched it with their hands﴾. If someone says: why did He not say, "they saw it with their eyes"? It is said: because touching is more effective in producing certainty than sight, for magic applies to what is seen but does not apply to what is touched; for what is touched becomes seen, but what is seen does not become touched. So He mentioned touching so that it would be more emphatic.

﴿Those who disbelieved would certainly say, "This is nothing but obvious magic."﴾ Its meaning: nothing benefits them. Even if We sent down to them what they proposed, they would say, "This is nothing but obvious magic."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 8:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they say: "Why has an angel not been sent down to him?"﴾ This is the statement of ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Umayya al-Makhzumi, who proposed (iqtaraḥa) the sending down of an angel. ﴿And if We had sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided.﴾ Mujahid said: its meaning is: the Hour would have been established. It was also said: its meaning is: they would have been utterly destroyed by punishment. This is the custom of God regarding the disbelievers: whenever they propose a sign, and God gives it to them, and then they disbelieve in it, He destroys them with punishment, as with the people of Noah, ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Lot, and their like. ﴿Then they would not be respited﴾, i.e., they would not be given a reprieve.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And had We made him an angel, We would surely have made him a man﴾, meaning: in the form of a man, because a man is more at ease with a man and understands from him. Gabriel came to the Prophet in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi, and the two angels came to Dawud in the form of two men. ﴿And We would have covered over for them what they cover over﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Dahhak, and a group said: its meaning is: We would have confused for them what they confuse. Regarding its meaning there are two opinions. The first: they cast doubt upon their weak followers, so doubt is cast upon them just as they cast it; and an angel descends in the form of a living man, so it becomes confusing for them, and some of them say: he is an angel, and some of them say: he is not an angel. The second opinion: its meaning is: We would have led them astray by sending down an angel in the form of a man, just as they went astray before, meaning: even if they supposed that they would be guided by the sending down of an angel, the sending down of an angel would not prevent Us from leading them astray through it.

"Concerning His words, Exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, messengers before you were mocked﴾. The occasion of this (revelation) was that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and Abu Jahl, and they laughed and mocked him; so the verse was revealed as consolation for him. ﴿So there descended upon those who mocked﴾, i.e., there befell those who mocked ﴿among them﴾ what they used to ﴿mock at﴾, i.e., the consequence of what they used to mock at."

Almighty Allah says: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth⦆ This travel may be understood as travel by thought and reason, and it may be understood as travel on foot. ﴿Then observe how was the end of those who denied⦆, meaning: of those nations that came before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth? Say: To Allah.﴾ He commands the answer to be given immediately after the question, so that it is more forceful in effect and more emphatic as proof, for whoever asks another about something and then follows it with the answer, that has greater effect. ﴿He has prescribed for Himself mercy.﴾ That is: (decreed). It is authentically related through the narration of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah wrote a book before He created the heavens and the earth, and it is with Him above His Throne: 'My mercy precedes My wrath.'"

﴿That He will surely gather you﴾ the lam is the lam of oath, meaning: "By Allah, He will surely gather you." ﴿On the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.﴾ That is: there is no doubt about it. ﴿Those who have lost their souls, they do not believe.﴾ (They have cheated themselves.)

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And His is whatever dwells in the night and the day﴾. It has been said: there is an ellipsis in it, and its meaning is: "And His is whatever rests and whatever moves." It has also been said that it refers to rest specifically, and rest was singled out because the blessing lies more in rest than in movement. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 14:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth?﴾ Fatir (al-Fatir): the Creator, the One who brings creation into being. Al-Asma'i said: I did not know the meaning of fatir until two Bedouins came to me disputing over a well. One of them said: "I am its fatir (fatartuhu)," and the other said: "I am its fatir." So I knew that it means the bringing of creation into being. ﴿And He feeds but is not fed.﴾ Al-A'mash recited: "wa huwa yut'imu wa la yut'am" with the yā' vowelled with a fatha, meaning: it is eaten but does not eat. As for the well-known recitation, its meaning is: He provides sustenance and is not provided for.

﴿Say: Indeed I have been commanded to be the first of those who submit (aslama).﴾ That is: of this community. Islam here means submission to the command of Allah, exalted is He. ﴿And never be among the polytheists.﴾ Although he is protected from shirk, the command to remain steadfast (bi-l-thabat) in faith and to abandon associating partners may be directed at him. It was also said: the address is to him, but what is meant is the community.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 15:

﴿He said: "Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day."﴾ That is: the punishment of the Resurrection (al-Qiyamah).

﴿Whoever is averted from it﴾ means: the punishment. Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Bakr, on the authority of ʿĀṣim, read "يَصْرِف" with a fatḥa on the yāʾ, meaning: whoever Allah averts the punishment from on that day. ﴿Then He has shown him mercy, and that is the clear success.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 17:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if Allah touches you with harm, there is none to remove it except Him﴾. Ḍurr (harm) is the opposite of benefit (nafʿ). Its meaning: if Allah afflicts you with harm, there is none to remove it except Him. ﴿And if He touches you with good, then He is over all things competent﴾.

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "I was riding behind the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: 'Shall I not teach you words through which you will benefit in this world and the Hereafter?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Guard Allah, and He will guard you...' [the report continues] until he said: 'If all creation gathered to benefit you with anything that Allah has not written for you, they would not be able to do it; and if they gathered to prevent you from anything that Allah has written for you, they would not be able to do it...'" — the report.

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And He is the Subduer (al-Qahir) over His servants﴾. Al-Qahir is the Dominant who cannot be overcome. It was also said: He is the One who alone administers affairs, compelling creation to His will. And His saying: ﴿over His servants﴾ refers to the attribute of Highness (al-istiʿla') that belongs to God, the Exalted, as known by the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah). ﴿And He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest in testimony?"﴾ The reason for this: the disbelievers said, "O Muhammad, who will testify to your truthfulness?" So the verse was revealed: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest in testimony?"﴾, meaning: from God. They used this as evidence that God is a "thing" (shay'). ﴿Say: "God is witness between me and you."﴾ That is: He testifies for me to the truth, and against you for falsehood.

﴿And this Qur'an has been revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches.﴾ That is: whomever the Qur'an reaches until the Hour arrives. In a report from the Prophet (ﷺ): "May God make radiant the face of a man who heard a saying from me, memorized it, and then conveyed it; for many a bearer of knowledge is more retentive than its hearer." It was also said: its meaning is, "that I may warn you thereby," meaning the Arabs, "and whomever it reaches," meaning the non-Arabs (ʿajam).

﴿Do you indeed testify that there are other gods along with God?" Say, "I do not testify." Say, "He is only one God, and I am free of what you associate with Him."﴾ He commanded him to answer immediately after the question, for the reason we have explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 20:

﴿Those to whom We have given the Book recognize it as they recognize their own sons.﴾ It has been said: by this is meant Muhammad (ﷺ). And it has been said: by this is meant the Qur'an, which they recognize ﴿as they recognize their own sons﴾.

﴿Those who have lost their souls, they do not believe.﴾ That is: they have cheated themselves (ghabanu anfusahum, from ghabn, "a loss through unfair dealing"). Their cheating is that they have lost the capital. And it is related in a report (khabar) that God, may He be exalted, created for every human being a dwelling place in Paradise; if he disbelieves, he loses those dwelling places, and God, may He be exalted, gives them to the believer.

Almost identical request; translate faithfully.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies His verses?﴾ That is: he attributes to Him what He did not say. ﴿Or denies His verses﴾ means: the verses of the Qur'an. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾

Allah's statement: ﴿And the Day We gather them all﴾. He meant by it: the gathering of the Resurrection. ﴿Then We will say to those who associated partners [with Allah]: "Where are your partners that you used to claim?"﴾ That is, where are the partners that you used to claim were partners of Allah? And "zaʿm" (claim) is a statement of falsehood. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "Zaʿm" means falsehood in every context. And in the reports: "They claimed" is the mount of falsehood (maṭiyyat al-kadhib).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 23:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then their fitnah (trial, or their excuse) was not but that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾ Qatadah said: its meaning is: "Then their excuse (ma'dhirah) was not..." Others said: "Then their speech was not..." except that they said.

Al-Zajjaj said: In His saying, ﴿Then their fitnah was not⁠﴾, there is a subtle meaning. It is like the man who is captivated (yuftan) by a beloved and then is afflicted with a trial because of it, so he disavows his beloved, and it is said: "His captivation was nothing but this." Likewise, the disbelievers, when they were captivated by love of the idols, then when they see the punishment, they disavow them.

Allah, exalted is He, says: {Then their fitnah was not but that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."}

﴿Look how they lied against themselves﴾. Their lying against themselves: their disavowal of shirk (associating partners with God). ﴿And what they used to fabricate vanished﴾, i.e., went away, ﴿from them﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 25:

The Most High said: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, but We have placed over their hearts coverings (akinna), so that they do not understand it, and in their ears a deafness.﴾ This refers to the leaders of the polytheists, such as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, while he was still a polytheist, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, 'Utba and Shayba, the two sons of Rabi'a, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, and others. They used to listen to the Qur'an. Then they said to Abu Sufyan: "What is this?" He said: "I see in it truth and falsehood." Abu Jahl said: "Until we have competed with one another in glory and been equal in renown, and the riding-camels have been equal among us, you claim that among you there is a prophet, O sons of 'Abd Manaf! By God, we will not acknowledge this." And in another narration: "Death is easier for us than this."

﴿And We have placed over their hearts coverings (akinna)﴾: it is the plural of kinan, just as a'inna is the plural of 'inan, and they are coverings. ﴿So that they do not understand it﴾: some of them said: "Lest they understand it (karaha an yafqahuhu)," and others said: "That they do not understand it (an la yafqahuhu)." ﴿And in their ears a deafness (waqran)﴾: that is, We placed deafness in their ears. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Waqr (heaviness) originally means weight, and from heaviness of the ear comes deafness."

﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾: this refers to the miracles of the Prophet and the signs that he showed them.

The Most High says: even if they see all those signs, they will not believe in them. It was also said: they proposed a particular sign, and then the words ﴿And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it﴾ were revealed. This applies to specific people whom God knew would not believe.

﴿Until, when they come to you disputing with you, those who disbelieve say: "This is nothing but the fables of the ancients."﴾ Their disputing was that they said to al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kalada, who had studied the revealed books and was among those who listened to the Qur'an: "What do you say about this?" He said: "This is nothing but the fables of the ancients," like the tales of Rustam and Isfandiyar, and the scriptures of the ancients. Tha'lab said: "Asatir is the plural of usturah, which means that which is written."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they forbid it and keep away from it﴾, meaning: they forbid the people from following Muhammad, and they keep themselves away from him. It was also said that the meaning of ﴿they forbid it﴾ is that they defend him and prevent the people from harming him, and ﴿they keep away from it﴾ means that they distance themselves from believing in him. This applies to Abu Talib, who used to defend him during his lifetime. Ibn ʿAbbas said: it was revealed concerning Abu Talib.

It is related that the leaders of Quraysh gathered around him and said to him: "Choose a young man of noble standing from among our people, adopt him as your son, and hand Muhammad over to us." Abu Talib said: "You have not been fair to me. I give you my son to be killed, and I raise your son?!"

It is also related that he said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Were it not that Quraysh would reproach me, I would have gladdened your eye with faith." He continued to defend him until he died. It is further related that he recited to Abu Talib the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they forbid it and keep away from it﴾, and Abu Talib said: "As for entering your religion, I will never enter it, but I will defend you as long as I live." He composed verses on this:

(By Allah, they will never reach you with their gathering
until I am laid in the dust, buried.)

(So proclaim your command, and there is no shame for you in it,
and rejoice in that, and let your eyes be cooled.)

(You called me, and I knew that you are my sincere advisor,
and you spoke the truth to me, and you were indeed trustworthy.)

(And I know well that the religion of Muhammad
is the best religion of mankind in faith.)

(Were it not for the fear of blame or dread of reproach,
you would have found me generous in declaring that openly.)

﴿And they destroy none but themselves﴾, meaning: the consequence of their deeds returns only upon themselves, ﴿and they perceive not﴾.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand over the Fire﴾, meaning: when they have entered the Fire. (It is also said: when they are presented before the Fire.) Al-wuquf (standing/being made to stand) means coming to know the reality of a thing. ﴿So they will say, "Oh, would that we could be returned"﴾ to the world ﴿"and not deny the signs of our Lord"﴾. Sibawayh said: this is the beginning of a statement, meaning: "We will never deny, whether we are returned or not." Others said: it is in continuation with what precedes it, i.e., "Oh, would that we could be returned and not deny the signs of our Lord," meaning: we will not disbelieve after being returned to the world. ﴿And that we might be among the believers﴾. It is also read "wa-nakūna" with a fatḥah on the nūn, and its implied sense is: "wa-li-nakūna min al-mu'minīn" (and so that we may be among the believers)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 28:

Allah's statement, the Exalted: ﴿Nay, but there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before﴾. His statement "bal" (nay, but) is purely a particle of retraction (bahta), a rebuttal of what they said. And His statement ﴿there has become apparent to them what they used to conceal before﴾ means: there has become apparent to them what they had concealed before, namely their disavowal of shirk by their saying: "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists." That is because when they say that, Allah seals their mouths, and their limbs speak of their shirk, so there becomes apparent to them what they used to conceal before.

﴿And even if they were returned, they would return to that which they were forbidden﴾. That is: even if they were returned to the world, they would revert to disbelief and to associating partners with Allah. ﴿And indeed, they are liars﴾, meaning: in their saying ﴿Oh, would that we were returned, and we would not deny the signs of our Lord﴾.

And in the reports it is related that Allah, the Exalted, will make an excuse to Adam on the Day of Resurrection with three excuses, the first of which is this, by His saying: "Indeed, I shall not admit from your offspring into the Fire except those whom I know that, if I returned them to the world seventy times, they would disbelieve in Me."
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "There is only our life of this world, and we will not be resurrected."﴾ This is about their denial of the Resurrection and the Last Day.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 30:

The words of His, the Exalted: ﴿And if you could see when they are made to stand before their Lord﴾, meaning: they are presented before their Lord. ﴿He will say, "Is this not the truth?"﴾, and that will be when the unseen matters and the hidden secrets are laid bare [for them].

﴿They will say, "Yes, by our Lord."﴾ So they acknowledge it. Ibn 'Abbas said: this is in one station, and His words ﴿"By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ are in another station, for there are many stations on the Day of Resurrection: in one station they deny, and in another station they acknowledge. ﴿He will say, "Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 31:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who denied the meeting with God have certainly lost﴾, meaning: they have lost themselves by their denial of the return to God; so "the meeting" here means the return to Him. ﴿Until, when the Hour comes upon them suddenly﴾, meaning: unexpectedly. ﴿They say, "Oh, our regret!"﴾ This is an intensification, like their saying "Oh, how strange!" (yā ʿajaban). The speaker's "Oh, how strange!" is more emphatic than his saying "I am amazed"; likewise His saying ﴿Oh, our regret!﴾ is more emphatic than saying "I am full of regret." Sibawayh said: this is in the form of a vocative, as if it says: "O regret, this is your time; O wonder, your time has come."

﴿Over what we neglected concerning it﴾, meaning: we fell short in it, that is, in the matter of the Resurrection. ﴿And they bear their burdens upon their backs.﴾ The awzār (burdens) are the loads; its singular is wizr, and from it comes the word wizr (a refuge/shelter), which is the "mountain" in His saying, exalted is He: {No! There is no refuge (wizr)}, meaning: no mountain and no place of safety. Their bearing of burdens is explained in the report which is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection. Whoever was righteous among them will meet a beautiful form with a pleasant fragrance, and it will say: 'Do you not recognize me? I am your good deed; mount me, for you have long ridden me.' And whoever was wicked will meet an ugly form with a foul smell, and it will say: 'Do you not recognize me? I am your evil deed, and you have long ridden me; so today I will ride you.'" This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And they bear their burdens upon their backs. Unquestionably, evil is what they bear.﴾
﴿Wa-ma al-hayat al-dunya illa la'ibun wa-lahwun, wa-lal-dar al-akhirah khayrun lilladhina yattaquna, afala ta'qilun﴾ [Qur'an 6:32]. He described both abodes in this verse.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We certainly know that what they say saddens you. It is not you they deny, but it is the signs of Allah that the wrongdoers reject.﴾ The occasion of revelation for this is that: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by Abu Jahl, who said: 'O Muhammad, you are truthful among us, but we deny what you have brought.'" This is the meaning of the verse. It was also said: this was revealed only as consolation for the Messenger (ﷺ). Allah, exalted is He, says: Do not grieve, for they do not deny you. It is also recited as "fa-innahum la yukadhdhibunaka" (with the verb lightened, i.e. without the doubling of the dal), and the difference between al-takdhib (taktheeb, calling someone a liar) and al-ikdhab (ikdhab, finding someone to be a liar) is this: al-takdhib is that one says to him, "You have lied," while al-ikdhab is that one finds him to be lying.

"The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And indeed messengers were denied before you, but they patiently bore the denial and the harm until Our help came to them. There is none who can alter the words of Allah.﴾ In it there is an ellipsis (hadhf), and its estimated form is: And indeed messengers were denied before you, and you were harmed, so they patiently bore what they were denied and were harmed. ﴿...until Our help came to them. And there is none who can alter the words of Allah.﴾ That is: the knowledge of Allah and His rulings. ﴿And there has certainly come to you some of the news of the messengers.﴾ That is: the reports of the messengers."

The Lord, exalted is He, says: "And if their turning away is heavy upon you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky to bring them a sign..." (6:35).

Al-nafq: a passage (sarab) in the earth. From it comes al-nafqa', which is the burrow of the jerboa (yarbu'). From it also comes nifaq (hypocrisy), because the hypocrite enters two tunnels (nafaqayn).

"Or a ladder into the sky [then bring them a sign]": i.e., a stairway into the sky, so that you bring them a sign. The cause of this: the disbelievers used to propose signs, and the Prophet (ﷺ) wished that God would give them what they proposed of signs, out of eagerness (tama') that they would see the signs and thereby submit. So there was revealed His saying: "If you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky to bring them a sign." Its meaning is: if you are able to do that, then do it, and there is an ellipsis (hadhf) in it.

"And if God had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance": i.e., by showing them a sign that would compel them to believe in it. The correct view, however, is that what is meant is: if God had willed, He would have fashioned and created them upon belief. This is closer to the position of the People of the Sunna (Ahl al-Sunna), because compelled belief (iman al-darura) does not benefit, and only belief in the unseen by free choice benefits. "So do not be among the ignorant": i.e., because of this matter, and that is His saying: "And if God had willed, He would have gathered them upon guidance."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Only those who listen will respond﴾. Here is the pause (waqf, a stopping point in recitation), and its meaning: Only those who listen will respond, those who listen with the listening of acceptance. ﴿As for the dead, God will raise them up﴾, meaning: the disbelievers. {then

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah is able to send down a sign"﴾. He means: He is able to send down signs. He has indeed sent down many signs and miracles, but He does not send down signs according to the demands of the disbelievers. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you﴾. He specified flying "with its two wings" only for emphasis. ﴿But they are communities like you﴾, meaning: kinds like you. In a report: "Were it not that dogs are a community, I would have commanded you to kill them. So kill every black dog that is completely black, for it is a devil." The meaning of the verse is that they are like you in creation, death and resurrection: He creates them as He creates you, causes them to die as He causes you to die, and raises them as He raises you. It has also been said that the meaning of His saying ﴿communities like you﴾ is in knowledge of what harms and benefits, in guarding against destruction, and in recognizing an enemy.

﴿We have not neglected anything in the Book﴾. If someone says: we see many rulings that are not in the Book, so what is the meaning of His saying ﴿We have not neglected anything in the Book﴾? It is said: there is nothing except that its root is in the Book. It is also said: what the Messenger said, he said from the Book, because he (ﷺ) has said in a well-known report: "I have been given the Qur'an and its like with it." And God, may He be exalted, has said: {Nor does he speak from desire; it is nothing but revelation that is revealed}. So everything established by the Sunnah is, as it were, established in the Book. It has also been said: [its meaning is]: We have not neglected anything in the Book of which there is need.

﴿Then to their Lord they will be gathered﴾. There is no doubt about the gathering of beasts and animals on the Day of Resurrection, to the point that it has been narrated that God, may He be exalted, will gather them and will exact retribution for the hornless from the horned. Abu Dharr narrated that the Prophet saw two sheep butting each other, and said: "O Abu Dharr, do you know why they are butting?" I said: "No." He said: "But God knows, and He will judge between them. And there are many like this." The way of people is to believe in it and leave its knowledge to God, may He be exalted, for it is something the intellects cannot reach. Concerning this verse there is an account: it is related that Bahlul the madman met Abu Yusuf the judge on the road, and asked him, saying: God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿There is no creature on the earth, nor a bird that flies with its two wings, but they are communities like you﴾, then He says: ﴿And there is no community but a warner has passed among them﴾. So what is the warner of the dogs? Abu Yusuf was perplexed and could not answer. Bahlul took a stone from the ground and said: "This is the warner of the dogs."

"Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who deny Our signs are deaf and dumb, in darkness.﴾ That is: deaf to hearing the truth, and dumb from speaking the truth. ﴿Whomever Allah wills, He leaves astray; and whomever He wills, He places on a straight path.﴾"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Tell me, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you, or the Hour comes upon you, will you call upon other than Allah, if you are truthful?﴾ It has been said: "The punishment of Allah" is death. "Or the Hour comes upon you" means: the Resurrection. "Will you call upon other than Allah, if you are truthful?" This is a question meant as affirmation (istifham bi-ma'na al-taqrir), meaning: you call upon none but Allah. And by this He intends the situations of necessity (fi ahwal al-darurat), for the disbelievers in situations of necessity call upon Allah, exalted is He, as He said: ﴿And when a wave covers them like shadows, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 41:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Rather, it is Him you call upon﴾. This is an affirmation of what was asked about in the first verse, meaning: rather, you call upon God and do not call upon anyone else. ﴿So He removes what you call upon Him for, if He wills﴾. Here He restricts the answering of the supplication to His will, whereas He left it unrestricted in His saying: ﴿Call upon Me; I will respond to you﴾.

The scholars said: That too is restricted by the will, as evidenced by this verse.

﴿And you forget what you associate﴾. That is because, when they abandoned the idols in times of dire need and turned to calling upon God, it was as if they had forgotten what they were associating. There is a metaphor (majaz) in the verse, and the implied meaning of His saying ﴿So He removes what you call upon Him for﴾ is: so He removes the harm of what you call upon Him for.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 42:

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We had certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you, and We seized them with adversity and hardship﴾. Al-Ba'sa' (adversity): hunger and poverty. Al-Darra' (hardship): sickness and affliction in person and property.

﴿That perhaps they might humble themselves﴾. Al-Tadarru' (humbling oneself): asking with humility. Abu 'Ubayd related from al-Farra': "Fulan yatadarra' wa-yatasadda," meaning that he asked humbly and in supplication.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 43:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Why, when Our punishment came upon them, did they not humble themselves?﴾ That is: "Why did they not humble themselves?" (﴿When Our punishment came upon them﴾) but their hearts were hardened. Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj) said its meaning is: their hearts had become so hard that We sent messengers to them, showed them the signs, and seized them with misfortune and adversity, yet they did not humble themselves and did not turn back from what they were upon. ﴿And Satan made what they were doing seem fair to them﴾. That is: until they continued on in their deeds and their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 44:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened for them the gates of everything﴾. This is an opening of gradual enticement (istidraj) and deception (makr). In the reports it is said: "Whoever has the gate of a blessing opened for him and does not realise that it is a deception against him, has no sound judgement; and whoever is struck by hardship and does not realise that it is a consideration for his good, has no sound judgement," meaning in matters of religion.

﴿Until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given﴾. This is the joy of insolence (bataru), which is forbidden, like the joy of Qarun in what he had acquired of the world, until his people said to him: "Do not exult; indeed Allah does not love those who exult."

﴿We seized them suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly, ﴿and behold, they were in despair﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Those who have lost hope of any good coming." Abu 'Ubayda said: "The mubliss (one in despair) is the regretful, grieving one." Al-Farra' said: "He is the one who is silent and cut off from argument." They recited:

(O friend, do you recognise a faded trace?
He said: "Yes, I recognise it, and it has become despairing (ablasa).")

And another said:

(A king who, when the heedless gather at his door,
they are envious, and the one in despair (al-mutabalis) is spared from among them.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off.﴾ Al-dabir (the last remnant, the root): here it means the origin (al-asl), so that dabir carries the meaning of "the last" (al-akhar). From this is His saying (ﷺ): "Among the signs of the Hour is such-and-such, and they will not come to the prayer except dabara," meaning, "last" (akhira). ﴿And all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.﴾ Allah praised Himself for their destruction and extermination, and in this is our instruction to praise Allah for the destruction of the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah took away your hearing and your sight and sealed over your hearts, what god other than Allah could bring them back to you?﴾ He mentioned several things, then said: "could bring them back to you" (yatikum bihi). So they differed. Some of them (said) its meaning is: "could bring you that which was taken [away]." Others said: His saying "could bring you back to you" (yatikum bihi, with the pronoun "hi") refers to hearing specifically, and sight and hearts are subsumed within it. From this, some scholars went to the view that hearing is superior to the other senses, since He singled it out with the pronoun, and they said: it is like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah and His Messenger have more right that they should please Him﴾, where the pronoun "hu" (Him) refers to Allah, may He be exalted, and the Messenger is subsumed within it. ﴿Look how We vary the signs, then they turn away﴾, i.e., they turn aside.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if the punishment of Allah comes upon you﴾. Al-Farra' related from the Arabs that they say: "Ara'aytaka" (a'raytaka) means "akhbirni" (inform me), "Ara'aytumaa" (a'raytumaa) means "akhbirani" (inform the two of us), and "Ara'aytukum" (a'raytukum) means "akhbirouni" (inform me, plural); and "Ara'aytik" (a'raytik), addressed to a woman, means "akhbirini" (inform me). Likewise ﴿suddenly or openly﴾: its meaning is "at night or by day." It was also said: its meaning is "suddenly or visibly." ﴿Will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?﴾.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We do not send the messengers except as bearers of good news and warners.﴾ We have already explained this. ﴿So whoever believes and makes amends, there will be no fear for them, nor will they grieve.﴾ He means: on the Day of Resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 49:

﴿And those who denied Our signs, the punishment will touch them﴾, meaning: the torment of the Fire will befall them, ﴿because they used to defy [Allah's command]﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 50:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah﴾. This was revealed when they proposed signs (ayat), and they used to say: "We will not believe you until you send down to us a book from the heaven," and all the other signs they proposed. So there was revealed His saying: ﴿Say: I do not tell you that with me are the treasures of Allah﴾, so that I give you what you desire (﴿and I do not know the unseen﴾). The unseen (al-ghayb) is everything that is hidden from you, whether it is past or future. Of it, the past can be known by a person through the report of an informant and the like. As for the future, none knows it except Allah and a messenger whom He has chosen, as He said in Surah al-Jinn. His saying ﴿and I do not know the unseen﴾ contains an ellipsis (idmar), meaning: "and I do not know the unseen except what Allah has taught me." ﴿And I do not tell you that I am an angel﴾: He was commanded to say this only because an angel is able to do what a human cannot, and it was said: because an angel witnesses what a human does not witness. Some used this to argue for the superiority of the angels over humans, but there is no proof in it. Its meaning is what we have made clear.

﴿I only follow what is revealed to me. Say: Are the blind and the seeing alike?﴾ Qatadah said: "The disbeliever and the believer." Mujahid said: "The one who is astray and the one who is guided." It was also said: "The ignorant and the knowledgeable." ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And warn thereby﴾, i.e., frighten thereby ﴿those who fear that they will be gathered to their Lord﴾. It was said: they are the Muslims. And it was said: everyone among the Muslims and the People of the Book who believes in the Resurrection.

﴿They have no protector or intercessor besides Him, so that they may fear Allah⦆. If it is said: Do not the prophets and the saints intercede on the Day of Resurrection? Then what is the meaning of His saying: ﴿They have no protector or intercessor besides Him﴾? We say: its meaning is that there is no intercession except by His permission, and they (the prophets and saints) intercede only by His permission. Or this is a refutation of what they claimed, that the angels and the idols intercede for us.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 52:

His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening﴾. The occasion of revelation (sabab nuzul) of the verse: "The polytheists in Makkah came to the Messenger of Allah and said: 'You sit with the poor.' By this they meant Bilal, Suhayb, Ibn Mas'ud, Ammar ibn Yasir, Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, Mihja', and others like them from the poor among the People of the Bench (ahl al-Suffah). They said: 'If you drove them away, we would believe in you.' It was as though they disdained sitting with them. The Prophet (ﷺ) considered this, hoping for their faith, and so the verse was revealed." Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said: "The verse was revealed concerning me, Ibn Mas'ud..." and he counted a group. Mujahid said: the verse was revealed concerning Bilal and a group. There is another view: the verse was revealed in Madinah. It is narrated that al-Aqra' ibn Habis al-Tamimi and Uyayna ibn Hisn al-Fazari came to the Messenger of Allah; they were among the great disbelievers. They said: "We disdain sitting with these people, so if you set aside a gathering for us apart from them, we will believe in you." He considered this, hoping for their faith, and so the verse was revealed. According to this view, the verse is among the verses of Madinah that were revealed in Madinah (al-ayat al-mubayyinah allati nazalat bi'l-Madinah).

His saying: ﴿And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord﴾. The scholars differed concerning this "calling" (da'wah). Ibn 'Abbas said: its meaning is that they perform the five daily prayers. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: it is remembrance of Allah (dhikr Allah). Al-Dahhak said: it is all acts of obedience (kull al-ta'at).

His saying: ﴿seeking His Face﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, they seek Him through obedience, and they seek His pure Face. The Face (al-wajh) is an attribute of Allah, Exalted is He, without asking how (bila kayf); a Face unlike faces.

﴿So you would drive them away and thus be among the wrongdoers﴾. That is: if you drove them away. It was also said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse, and its construction is: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, seeking His Face, so you would be among the wrongdoers." Then He said: ﴿You are not accountable for their reckoning in any way, nor are they accountable for yours in any way﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 53:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We have tested some of them through others﴾ is the trial of the wealthy through the poor, [and Allah, exalted is He, tests the wealthy through the poor], and He tests the poor through the wealthy. What is meant here is the trial of their elders through their poor: since they refused to believe because of them, and that was a trial for them.

﴿And [so] that they may say: "Are these the ones on whom Allah has bestowed favour from among us?"﴾ The wealthy say: "Have these poor people outstripped us in faith?" Then Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Is not Allah most knowing of those who are grateful?﴾ That is: Is not Allah most knowing of who is deserving of Islam, so that he enters into Islam? !

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 54:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when those who believe in Our signs come to you﴾ are the poor whom we mentioned, ﴿say: Peace be upon you.﴾ He commanded His Messenger to begin them with the greeting of peace (al-salam). We have already mentioned the meaning of peace (al-salam) earlier. It has also been said that its meaning is: may Allah keep you safe (salamakum) in your religion. It has also been said that its meaning is safety (al-salamah) for you.

﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy﴾ meaning He has decreed mercy for you. ﴿That whoever of you does evil in ignorance⁠—﴾ meaning in error (khati'ah). We have already explained that every disobedient person is ignorant. ﴿Then repents after that and makes amends, indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ It is read as "annahu" and "fa-annahu", both with the alif pointed with fatha; in that case it is a substitute (badal) for His saying: ﴿Your Lord has prescribed for Himself mercy.﴾ It is also read, both with the alif pointed with kasra, as a new sentence (ibtida'). And it is read: the first with fatha and the second with kasra.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We detail the verses, and that the way of the criminals may become clear﴾ is read in three ways: "ولتستبين" with a ta' (tastabīn), and "سَبِيل" with a fatha on the lam (sabīl). Its meaning: "that the way of the criminals may become clear, O Muhammad." If it is said: "Was it not already clear to him?" It is said: its meaning is "so that you may increase in clarity." Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj) said: the address is to the Messenger, and what is meant by the verse is the Community (ummah).

It is also read "وليستبين" with a ya' and a ta' ("and that it may become clear"), with "سَبِيل" in the nominative (sabīlu). They said: this is because the sabīl (way) is both masculine and feminine in usage. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Say: This is my way﴾. Its meaning: "and that the way of the criminals may become manifest." (If it is said: why was the way of the criminals singled out?) It is said: its estimated reading is: "that the way of the criminals and the way of the believers may become clear," so one of them was omitted for brevity. The more sound view is that its estimated reading is: "that the way of the criminals may become distinct from the way of the believers."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those whom you invoke besides God﴾ is the prohibition of associating partners with God (shirk). ﴿Say: I will not follow your desires; I would then have gone astray, and I would not be among the guided.﴾ It means: if I were to follow your desires,

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 57:

The Most High said: ﴿Say: Indeed I am upon clear evidence from my Lord﴾ (upon a clarification from my Lord), ﴿but you have denied it﴾, that is, what I have [brought]. ﴿What you seek to hasten is not with me﴾. It was said: he meant by it their seeking to hasten the signs and miracles. It was also said: he meant by it their seeking to hasten the Hour, as the Most High said: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it﴾. It was also said: he meant by it their seeking to hasten the punishment, as the Most High said: "They ask you to hasten the punishment." They used to say: ﴿If this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾.

﴿Indeed, judgment belongs only to Allah. He decides the truth, and He is the best of deciders﴾. It is also read as "yaqussu" with a ṣād, and he cited in support the writing in the codices (al-maṣāḥif), for this word is written without a yā'.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 58:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: If what you are impatient for were with me, the matter would have been decided between me and you﴾. Its meaning: the Resurrection would have been established. It has also been said: it concerns the punishment, and its meaning is: If the punishment were in my hand, I would have hastened it, so that I might be rid of you. ﴿And God knows best the wrongdoers﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 59:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him﴾. Ibn ʿUmar narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The keys of the unseen are five," and he mentioned the five referred to in His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah has knowledge of the Hour﴾, and then he recited the verse. ﴿And He knows what is on the land and in the sea﴾. Mujahid said: "The sea" here refers to the towns and cities, while "the land" refers to the deserts. It is said: "This city is a sea" and "this village is a sea," because of their gathering and the multitude of their people. It was also said: it is the land and the well-known sea.

﴿And not a leaf falls but He knows it﴾. If someone says: why did He single out the falling leaf, when He knows both the fallen and the attached? It is said: its meaning is: and not a leaf falls but He knows it, whether fallen or attached. Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq said: by the fallen leaf he meant the miscarried fetus (al-saqt).

﴿Nor a grain in the darknesses of the earth﴾. It is the well-known grain. Jaʿfar al-Sadiq said: it is the child (in the womb). ﴿Nor anything fresh or dry﴾. It was said: its meaning is: nor anything living or dead. It was also said: it is an expression for everything. ﴿But it is in a clear Book﴾, meaning: all of it is written in the Preserved Tablet. This is like His words: ﴿And every small and great thing is inscribed﴾.

﴿He it is who takes you in death by night﴾, that is, He seizes your souls by night when you sleep. This is similar to His saying: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death, and those that have not died during their sleep﴾. If someone says: Is not the soul of the one who sleeps still with him? So what is the meaning of this seizing? It is said: it is the seizing of the discerning, active soul. ﴿And He knows what you have earned by day﴾, that is, what you have done by day. ﴿Then He raises you up therein﴾. Qatada said: the raising up (al-ba'th) here is waking, that is, He wakes you up during the day. ﴿That a term appointed may be fulfilled﴾. Al-qada' is the final determination of a judgment in full, and its meaning here is the complete fulfilment of the appointed term of life.

(﴿Then to Him is your return; then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾.)

"The Exalted has said: ﴿And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardians﴾. As for the meaning of 'the Subduer' (al-Qahir) and the attribute of 'above' (al-fawq), we have already mentioned them. As for the sending of the guardians (al-hafazah), it is the sending of the angels who guard, and this is what He said in another verse: ﴿And indeed, over you are guardians, noble recorders﴾, and He said: ﴿For him there are successive [angels] before him and behind him, who guard him by the command of Allah﴾. Their guarding is that they guard over the servants their deeds, their term, and their provision. ﴿Until, when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him in death﴾, and it is read 'tawaffathu' [with 'yā' rather than 'tā'] — "tuwaffīhi" with a yā. ﴿And they do not fall short﴾, meaning: they do not delay.

If it is said: He said in another verse: ﴿Say: The angel of death will take you in death﴾, and here He said: ﴿Our messengers take him in death﴾, so how is the reconciliation? It is said: Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: The angel of death has helpers from among the angels who take souls by his command; this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Our messengers take him in death﴾. And the angel of death is in reality the one who takes souls, since they act upon his command, and for that reason the action was attributed to him in that verse. It is also said: its meaning is: the singular is mentioned with a plural expression, and what is intended is the angel of death. In the narratives it is related that Allah, the Exalted, made the world before him like a small tray; so he takes [souls] from here and from there, and when the spirits become numerous, he calls the spirits and they respond to him."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 62:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then they will be returned to Allah, their true Master (mawlahum al-haqq)﴾. If someone says: the verse concerns both the believers and the disbelievers, so how does He say ﴿their true Master﴾, when He says in another verse: ﴿And that the disbelievers have no mawla (protector/master)﴾? It is said: the word mawla in that verse means "helper (al-nasir)", and there is no helper for the disbelievers; whereas mawla here means "owner (al-malik)", and Allah is the owner of all things. It is also said: He intended by it the return of the believers to Him, and the disbelievers are included in it by implication.

﴿Surely judgment belongs to Him, and He is the swiftest of reckoners﴾, i.e., He reckons all of them in an instant.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 63:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Who delivers you from the darknesses of the land and the sea?﴾ means: from the hardships of the sea and the land. The Arabs say, "A dark day" (yawm mudhlim) when it is a day of hardship, and they also call it "a day with stars" (yawman dha kawkab). It is as if they made it like the night because of its severity. The poet said:

(Banu Asad, do you know our affliction
on a day that has stars, white-grey and fierce?)

And another said:

(My she-camel is a ransom for the Banu Dhuhl ibn Shaybān
on a day that has stars, most terrible.)

﴿Calling upon Him humbly and secretly﴾ means: openly and secretly. It was also said: its meaning is that the secret and the open are combined in the supplication, such that one calls with the tongue while the heart is with it. It is read "khufyatan" with a kasra on the kha', and both have the same meaning. ﴿If You deliver us from this, we will surely be among the thankful﴾. And gratitude (shukr) is: recognition of the blessing together with fulfilling its right, and both of these are necessary for gratitude to be realized.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 64:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: It is Allah who delivers you from it and from every distress; yet you associate partners with Him.﴾ Al-karb (distress): the utmost extent of anxiety.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 65:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: He is able to send upon you punishment from above you or from beneath your feet.﴾ Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan, Qatada and a group said: the verse was revealed concerning the people of faith and the people of prayer (ahl al-salat). Others said: it was revealed concerning the polytheists. As for His words ﴿punishment from above you or from beneath your feet﴾, Mujahid and Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: "punishment from above you" is being pelted with stones, as happened to the people of Lut, and "or from beneath your feet" is being swallowed up by the earth and the earthquake.

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "punishment from above you" is the domination of unjust leaders (aʾimmat al-su'), and "from beneath your feet" is the domination of wicked servants. It was also said: "punishment from above you" is the flood and drowning, and "from beneath your feet" is the wind, as happened to the people of ʿAd. ﴿Or confuse you into factions (shiya'an)﴾. al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is: He will mix you in a mixing of discord, not a mixing of agreement; the real meaning is that He will spread among you divergent desires, so that you become sects and parties.

(﴿and make some of you taste the violence of others﴾) is the occurrence of killing among them. It is authentically related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that when this verse was revealed and he heard the first part, he said: "I seek refuge in Your Face." When he heard the latter part, he said: "These two are easier." In the well-known report: "When this verse was revealed, he supplicated for his community and conversed at length, until Jibril came down saying that Allah had removed the first two, and answered your supplication concerning them, but did not grant it concerning the last." Thus desires and fighting spread among this community, and the sword has been drawn since the time of ʿUthman, and it will not be sheathed until the Hour arrives. It is also related that the well-known supplication which the Messenger of Allah used to make, he made when this verse was revealed, saying: "O Allah, I seek refuge in Your pardon from Your punishment, and I seek refuge in Your pleasure from Your anger, and I seek refuge in You from You," meaning: in Your decree from Your decree. ﴿See how We vary the signs﴾, meaning: once in this way, and once in that way, ﴿that they may understand﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 66:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿But your people have denied it, though it is the truth.﴾ That is, the Quran. ﴿Say, "I am not a guardian over you."﴾ That is, not one who has power over you, to compel you to Islam, whether you wish or refuse. Ibn Jurayj said: This was at the beginning, then it was abrogated (naskh) by His words: ﴿Then kill the polytheists﴾.

For every news there is a fixed time (mustaqarr), and you will come to know it. Mujahid said: its meaning is that every report of the reports of the Qur'an has a reality (haqiqa), either in this world or in the Hereafter. "And you will come to know."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 68:

The words of God, exalted is He: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them﴾. He meant by it: those who engage in them with rejection and mockery. Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir said: "This also includes engaging in [discussion of] all verses not in accordance with the Book and the Sunnah."

﴿So turn away from them until they engage in a conversation other than this. And if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾. He means by His words: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them﴾. The Companions said: "How, then, can we sit in the Sacred Mosque and how can we circumambulate the House, while they are engaged in vain talk constantly?" So this verse was revealed.

Surah 6, verse 69: "And upon those who fear Allah is nothing of their account [responsibility], [if they hold them to account]..." — wait, I need to translate the commentary text itself.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 69:

﴿And upon those who are mindful of Allah there is nothing of their reckoning whatever﴾, meaning: when they encounter them, and they do not plunge into what they plunge into. ﴿But it is a reminder, that they may be mindful﴾. He commanded [reminding them] and forbade them from that. It was also said: its meaning is: in the state of remembrance, and there is nothing upon them in the state in which they remind them, if they are not pleased with what they plunged into.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 70:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And leave those who have taken their religion as amusement and diversion, and whom the worldly life has deceived.﴾

Al-Farra' said in his book: "Every religious community's festival (ʿīd) is a day of amusement and play, except the festival of the Muslims, for it is a day of prayer, doing good, and glorifying God (takbīr)."

﴿And remind by it, lest a soul be delivered to ruin (tubsala) for what it has earned.﴾ Mujahid said: "Lest it be handed over to destruction." Qatadah said: "Lest it be detained." Al-Farra' said: "Lest it be held in pledge." Al-Kisa'i and al-Akhfash said: "Lest it be requited." The correct view is the first, as it is said: "So-and-so is mustabsil" when he has surrendered himself to destruction. The poet said:

(And my surrendering of my sons without a crime... [they were not returned, nor with blood spilled])

The real meaning is: remind by it, lest a soul be surrendered to ruin by its deeds. ﴿It shall have, besides God, no protector and no intercessor.﴾ We have already mentioned it. ﴿And if it offers every ransom, it will not be accepted from it.﴾ The ransom is what we mentioned. ﴿Those are the ones who were delivered to ruin for what they had earned; for them is a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment for what they used to disbelieve.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 71:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Shall we call upon, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit us nor harm us?"﴾ If it is said: how can they not harm them, when idols harm them? It is said: its meaning is that it does not bring about benefit, nor does it ward off harm. It is said: its meaning is that nothing is in their hands.

﴿And be turned back on our heels after Allah has guided us﴾, that is: turning back upon our heels after being guided to Him and to Islam. ﴿Like one whom the devils have enticed in the earth, bewildered﴾: the devils misled him and overpowered him until he fell (hawā), and the ḥayrān (bewildered) is one who wavers between two things, not knowing what to do.

﴿He has companions who call him to guidance, "Come to us."﴾ This is given as an example of one who apostatizes from Islam, by a man who is on the road with a company; the ghoul (ghūl) misleads him, and his companions from the company call him to the road, but he remains bewildered, not knowing where to go. (﴿Say: "Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] guidance, and we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."﴾)

[Translation]

"And that you establish the prayer and fear Him" (ﷺ-less): i.e., "We were commanded to establish the prayer and to be mindful of God (taqwa)." ﴿And it is He to whom you will be gathered﴾.

And He it is who created the heavens and the earth in truth (i.e., to manifest the truth), for He made His handiwork a proof of His oneness. ﴿And the day He says, "Be," and it is,﴾ It has been said that this refers back to His words ﴿created the heavens﴾, meaning: "and He created the day He says..." If it is asked, how can this interpretation be valid, since the Resurrection has not yet been created? It is answered: it exists in the knowledge of God, Exalted is He, so it is as though it were created, since creation (khalq) here means decree and determination, and it has been decreed and determined. It has also been said that the implied sense is: "Remember the day He says, 'Be,' and it is." ﴿His word is the truth; and His is the dominion on the day the Trumpet is blown.﴾ It has been read in the irregular (shadhdh) readings: "the day it is blown into the Trumpet" (yawma yunfakhu fi al-sur), and the word ṣūr is the plural of ṣūrah. Abu 'Ubayda said: ṣūr is the same ṣūr in every place. Ibn Mas'ud, in his explanation of the verse, said: al-ṣūr is a horn that is blown into, and it is well known in the reports. ﴿Knower of the unseen and the visible; and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when Abraham said to his father Azar﴾. "Azar" is read with a raised ra' (ḍamma), which is among the shādhdh (irregular, non-canonical) readings, and its meaning is: "O Azar." Likewise in the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "O Azar." The well-known reading is "Azar" with a fatḥa on the ra', and it is a non-Arabic proper noun (ism a'jamī) that is not declined (ghayr munṣarif); so it takes a fatḥa in the position of the genitive (khafḍ).

Al-Farrā' and al-Zajjāj said: the name of his father was Tārikh, on which the genealogists agree, and Āzar is a title (laqab) for him. Al-Farrā' said: the title has come to dominate over the name. It was also said: he had two names, Āzar and Tārikh. Al-Ḥasan said: his name is Āzar only, not otherwise, as is stated in the Book. Mujāhid said: Āzar is the name of an idol.

The meaning of the verse is: "And when Abraham said to his father: ﴿Do you take﴾ Azar ﴿idols as gods? Indeed I see you and your people in clear error.﴾"

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 75:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And thus did We show Abraham the dominion (malakut) of the heavens and the earth﴾. Malakut and malk (dominion) are one and the same, and the ta' was added to it for emphasis, like rahbut and rahmut. They differed over its meaning. Some said: He showed him the gates of the heavens and the earth. Others said: The heavens were opened for him until he saw them all and what is in them, and the earths were pierced for him until he saw them all. It was also said: He raised him up to the heaven until he saw the heavens and the earth.

And in the report: "When He raised him up to the heaven, he saw a man on the earth committing an act of disobedience, so he prayed to Allah until He destroyed him. Then he saw another, and he prayed to Allah until He destroyed him. Then he saw a third doing likewise, and he prayed to Allah until He destroyed him. Then the Exalted said: Bring him down. Then the Exalted revealed to him: Gently, O Abraham, for My servants are of three kinds in My sight: either they repent, and I forgive them; or they leave behind a child who prays for them, and I forgive them; and if they have none [to pray for them], then Hell is behind them." ﴿And that he might be among the certain (muqinin)﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 76:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So when the night covered him, he saw a star.﴾

In the narrative: one of the soothsayers (kahanah) said to Nimrod, "Your kingdom will be destroyed at the hands of a boy born in your time." So he would kill the boys born in his time. When Abraham's mother bore Abraham, his father took him to a cave-like hollow in the earth (sarb al-ard, shibh maghar) and placed him in a place called Kuthaa. It was said that he remained there for seven years, and it was said thirteen years, and it was said seventeen years. Then, when he grew up, he said to his mother, "Who is my Lord?" She said to him, "Be quiet." Then she came and informed his father of what he had said. His father came, and Abraham said to him, "Who is my Lord?" He said, "Your mother." He said, "And who is my mother's lord?" He said, "I am." He said, "And who is your lord?" He said, "Be quiet," and they left him. Then, when the night covered him, he went out of the hollow, having never seen anything before, and he saw a star. It was said: it was Jupiter.

As-Suddi said: the star was Venus, and it is the brightest star in the sky. ﴿He said, "This is my lord."﴾ It was said: he said this in his childhood, when his words were not regarded. And it was said: he was only reasoning by means of it, and he said this in the state of reasoning, so this statement did not harm him. These two sayings are weak. In this verse there are three well-known opinions:

The first: Qutrub said: his saying "This is my lord" is in the form of a question, and its implied meaning is "Is this my lord?" A similar example is the saying of the poet:

(They rebuked me and said, "O Khuwaylid, do not be alarmed,"
so I said, and the faces denied them, "They are they.")

He said "they are they" as a question, and its implied meaning is "Are they they?" As for az-Zajjaj and others, they did not accept this, and they said: in the speech of the Arabs, "hadha" (this) does not carry the meaning of a question.

Az-Zajjaj mentioned two other opinions concerning it. The first: he said, "This is my lord" according to the claim of his people. If it is said: they used to worship the stars, so how did he say it according to their claim? It is answered: some of them were astrologers, and they held that affairs were referred to the stars; so it was as if they worshipped the stars.

The second opinion: the saying is implied within it, and its implied meaning is: "They say: This is my lord."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 77:

﴿So when it set, he said: "I do not love those that set."﴾

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿When he saw the moon rising﴾, meaning: rising (ṭāliʿan), ﴿he said: "This is my lord."﴾ That happened on a night in which the moonrise was delayed a little. ﴿Then when it set, he said: "If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray."﴾ Al-ufūl (ُالأفول) is al-ghurūb (the setting).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 78:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater."﴾ That is: brighter and more luminous. If someone says: Why did he say "This is my lord," when the sun (al-shams) is feminine, and why did he not say "this one" (hadhihi)? It is said: because that which does not bear the sign of the feminine may be used in the masculine, as the poet said:

(Neither a cloud, when it has rained its rain, nor a land whose plants have sprouted its herbage...)

He did not say "has sprouted" (abqalat), although the land (al-ard) is feminine, because it did not bear the sign of the feminine. It is also said: his saying "This is my lord" refers to the meaning, which is light and radiance. ﴿Then when it set, he said, "O my people, I am free of what you associate [with God]."﴾

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who created the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.﴾ Ḥanīf (one who turns away from falsehood toward pure monotheism): one who is firm upon the religion, inclining toward it entirely.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 80:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And his people argued with him. He said: "Do you argue with me concerning Allah when He has already guided me?"﴾ (i.e.) his people disputed with him; he said: "Do you dispute with me?" ﴿concerning Allah, when He has already guided me.﴾

﴿And I do not fear what you associate with Him.﴾ This is because they used to frighten him with the idols, and they would say: "Beware of the idols, for we fear that they will afflict you with madness and insanity." So he said: ﴿And I do not fear what you associate with Him, unless my Lord wills something.﴾

His saying: "unless my Lord wills something." It is not an exception from the first clause, since it is not permissible that Allah should will that anything from the idols or what they associate with Him should afflict him. Rather, this is an exception of disconnection (istithna' munqati'), and its meaning is: "But if my Lord wills that He take me by something, or punish me for my sin, then that is His to do."

﴿My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Will you not then be mindful?﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 81:

The words of His, exalted is He: ﴿And how should I fear what you have associated [with Allah], while you do not fear that you have associated with Allah that for which He has not sent down to you any authority?﴾ Al-ishrak (association): it is the joining of two things in one meaning. So, ishrak with Allah is that one joins with Allah other than Allah in that which is not permissible except for Allah. The meaning of the verse: How should I fear the idols which you have associated, when you are more deserving of fear from me, since you have associated [others] with Allah, and you do not fear Allah for your association or your deed for which Allah has sent down no proof or authority? ﴿So which of the two parties is more deserving of security?﴾ meaning, the monotheist or the polytheist? ﴿If you should know.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 82:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who believe and do not mix their belief with wrongdoing﴾. Scholars differed regarding this. Some said: this is from the speech of God, exalted is He. It was also said: it is from the speech of Ibrahim (Abraham), and its meaning is: those who believe and do not mix their belief with polytheism (shirk). This is the view of Abu Bakr, Ali, Hudhayfah, and Salman, that the intended meaning of "wrongdoing" (zulm) is shirk. It is authentically reported through the narration of Ibn Mas'ud that when this verse was revealed, it weighed heavily upon the Companions, and they said: "Which of us has not wronged himself?" He said: "The matter is not as you think. Rather, wrongdoing here means shirk," and he recited the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿Do not associate partners with God; indeed, association is a great wrongdoing﴾. The meaning of the verse is: those who believe in God and do not associate anything with Him, ﴿for them is security, and they are the guided﴾.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on Surah 6, verse 83:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that was Our argument which We gave Abraham against his people.﴾ Scholars differed about it. Some said: it is his argument against them with his saying: ﴿So which of the two parties is more worthy of security?﴾ His proof for this is that one who worships Allah and does not associate anything with Him is more worthy of security than one who worships Allah and associates others with Him. It was also said: He meant by it the argument with which Nimrod argued, as has preceded in Surat al-Baqarah.
