﴿We raise in degrees whom We will.﴾ That is: through argument (al-hijaj) and reasoning (al-istidlal). It is also read as "نرفع دَرَجَات" with tanwin (nunation) on "دَرَجَات", and its meaning would be: We raise whom We will to degrees. ﴿Indeed your Lord is Wise and Knowing.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 84:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob; each We guided, and Noah We guided before, and of his descendants﴾ — the scholars differed concerning this. Some of them said: He meant by it the descendants of Abraham. The correct view is that He meant by it: "and of the descendants of Noah," because He counted in the same passage Yunus (Jonah) and Lut (Lot), and they are of the descendants of Noah, not of the descendants of Abraham. ﴿And of his descendants: Dawud (David), Sulayman (Solomon), Ayyub (Job), Yusuf (Joseph), Musa (Moses), and Harun (Aaron). Thus do We reward the doers of good.﴾ This is not in the order of the times, since these were in different eras, some preceding others. The particle "wa" (and) does not necessitate sequence; it is only for joining together.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 85:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And Zakariyya and Yahya and Isa﴾. This is evidence that Isa is among the descendants of Adam, even though his lineage is traced to the mother; for He counted him among the descendants of Nuh, so Adam is his father from the mother's side. ﴿And Ilyas, each of them is among the righteous﴾. Ibn Mas'ud said: Ilyas is Idris, but the correct view is that he is another man.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 6, verse 86:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Isma'il and al-Yasa'﴾. It is also read "wal-Laysa'". It is a non-Arabic (a'jami) name, like Zayd, Yazid, and the like. The definite article "al-" is attached to it only rarely. A similar case is the saying of the poet:

(We found "al-Walid ibn al-Yazid" blessed, ... his shoulders heavy with (the burdens) of the caliphate.)

﴿And Yunus and Lut, and each We preferred over the worlds.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 87:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And of their fathers﴾. The "min" (from) here is for partitive meaning (li-l-tab'id), because the fathers of some of them were Muslims and guided. ﴿And their offspring﴾, meaning: and of their offspring. By this he also intends the offspring of some of them, because ʿIsa and Yahya had no offspring, and among the offspring of some of them there were those who were disbelievers. ﴿And their brothers, and We chose them﴾, meaning: We selected them. ﴿And We guided them﴾, meaning: We directed them ﴿to a straight path﴾.

That is the guidance of Allah; He guides with it whomever He wills among His servants. ﴿And if they had associated others with Allah, what they used to do would have been lost from them.﴾ That is, it would have been nullified for them. Ihbat (ḥubūṭ, nullification, invalidation) means butlān (nullity, becoming void), and this is like His saying: ﴿If you associate others with Allah, your deeds will surely be lost.﴾

These are the ones to whom We gave the Book (al-Kitab): a generic noun (ism al-jins), and by it he means the scriptures revealed to them, ﴿and the judgment﴾, meaning: knowledge and understanding (al-fiqh), ﴿and prophethood. So if these disbelieve in them, We have already entrusted them to a people who are not disbelievers in them﴾, meaning: the people of Madinah, and those among them of the Emigrants (al-Muhajirin) and the Helpers (al-Ansar). Qatadah said: "﴿So if these disbelieve in them﴾ means: the disbelievers, ﴿We have already entrusted them to a people﴾ meaning: the prophets mentioned earlier, ﴿who are not disbelievers in them﴾." Abu Raja' al-Utaridi said: its meaning is: "If the people of the earth disbelieve in them, We have entrusted them to the people of the heavens, who are the angels, ﴿who are not disbelievers in them﴾."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 90:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those are the ones whom God guided﴾, meaning: God guided them. ﴿So follow their guidance﴾. This is the hā' of pause (hā' al-waqf), as in His saying: ﴿Mā liyah﴾ and ﴿sulṭāniyah﴾, and similar to that. It is also read: "fa-bihudāhum iqtadih" with a kasra on the hā', and its implied meaning is: "fa-bihudayhim iqtadi iqtidā'" (so follow their guidance with following). It has been said: the verbal noun (maṣdar) is intended here, as in His saying: ﴿Say: I do not ask you for any reward for it; it is only a reminder (dhikr) to the worlds﴾, meaning: its reminder.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 91:

His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they did not magnify God with His true magnification. Abu 'Ubayda said: they did not know God with His true knowledge. Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said: they did not describe God with His true description. It is said: "I measured (qadartu) the thing and qadartuhu," meaning that when one knows its reality (haqiqah).

﴿When they said: God has not sent down anything to a human being﴾. It is said: this is the statement of Malik ibn al-Sayf, who was a rabbi (hibr) of the Jews. He argued with the Prophet, and in the course of the argument there slipped from his tongue: "God has not sent down anything to a human being." This took place in Mecca, and so this verse was revealed.

﴿Say: Who sent down the Book that Musa brought, a light and guidance for mankind?﴾ That is, answer them, O Muhammad, and say: Who sent down the Torah to Musa, while you believe in it?

In the narrative: the Jews heard from him that statement, so they reproached him and said: Did not God send down the Torah to Musa? Why then did you say, "God has not sent down anything to a human being"? Malik ibn al-Sayf said: Muhammad angered me, so I said what I said. They said: When you become angry, you say about God other than the truth. So they removed him from the rabbinate (al-hibriyya) and seated Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf in his place.

﴿You make it into parchments, displaying them﴾ That is, you make from them books that you display ﴿and you conceal much﴾ That is, you conceal what contains the description of Muhammad, and display from them what does not contain the description of Muhammad. ﴿And you were taught what you did not know, neither you nor your fathers﴾. It is said: this refers to the Jews. It is also said: it is an address to the Companions.

God, the Exalted, said (meaning: say: Who sent it down), and this refers back to what preceded: ﴿Say: God. Then leave them in their discourse, playing﴾. Everyone who engages in what does not benefit is a player (la'ib).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 92:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed﴾ describe the Qur'an as blessed. The root meaning of barakah (blessing) is permanence and stability, and from it comes the expression barak al-ba'ir (the camel kneeling down), when it settles and remains still. From the same root is His saying: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is the dominion﴾, meaning that what is due to Him of glorification and majesty is established for Him, in what has never ceased and never will cease.

﴿Confirming what was before it﴾, that is, of the Books revealed before it. ﴿And that you may warn the Mother of Towns﴾, that is, the people of Umm al-Qura, ﴿and those around it﴾. Umm al-Qura is Makkah. It was called Umm al-Qura because all the other towns [make for it and come to it]. It is also said that it was called this because the earth was spread out from beneath it, and it is also said that it was called this because it is revered and sought out with honour. From the same usage the mother is called umm (mother), because she is honoured. It has also been said: "Indeed Madinah is a town that devours all other towns," meaning that the people of Madinah overrun all other towns by the sword.

﴿And those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are over their prayers, guarding them.﴾

If it is asked: the Jews and the Christians believe in the Hereafter but do not believe in it (the Qur'an), so what is the meaning of His saying "And those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it"? It is answered: He meant by this the believers, for they are the ones who truly believe in the Hereafter. As for those who claim to believe in the Hereafter but do not affirm Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought, it is as though they have not truly believed in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 93:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or says, "It has been revealed to me," while nothing has been revealed to him?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "This was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh. He had embraced Islam, and the Prophet made him a scribe of the revelation, and he would dictate the revelation to him and he would write it down. It is said that he [the Prophet] would dictate to him, 'Indeed Allah is Hearing, Knowing,' and he would write, 'Indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful,' and [if] he dictated to him, 'Indeed Allah is Forgiving, Merciful,' he would write, 'Indeed Allah is Knowing, Wise.' This is how he would alter [the text]. It is narrated that when the words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a drop in a firm resting place﴾ (and the rest of the verse) were revealed, and the Prophet dictated that, [the man] marvelled at the detail of God's creation and said, 'Blessed is Allah, the best of creators.' The Prophet said to him, 'Thus it was revealed,' [quoting] ﴿So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾. The man doubted the revelation and said, 'It is revealed to me just as it is revealed to him,' and he apostatised from Islam." So His words ﴿or says, "It has been revealed to me"﴾ refer to this.

It is also said: the verse was revealed concerning Musaylima the Liar and al-Aswad al-'Ansi, who went out in Yemen, claimed prophethood and claimed that revelation came to them. It is narrated from the Prophet that he said: "I saw in a dream two gold bracelets on my hands, and I blew on them, and they flew away. I interpreted them as two liars who would emerge after me." Musaylima the Liar was in al-Yamama, and al-Aswad al-'Ansi was in Sana'a of Yemen.

﴿And who says, "I will reveal the like of what Allah has revealed"﴾ This is concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kalada, who claimed to produce a counterpart to the Qur'an. It is narrated that he said, in attempting to counter the Qur'an: "By the grinding ones, grinding [flour]; by the kneading ones, kneading; by the baking ones, baking; by the morsel-making ones, making morsels."

﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death﴾ meaning: in the severities of death. The poet said:

(The agonies, then you will be relieved... then you will go away and not return to us)

﴿and the angels are extending their hands﴾ It is said: to punish; and it is said: to seize the souls. ﴿"Bring out your souls"﴾ meaning: your spirits. If someone says: the spirit only leaves unwillingly, so what is the meaning of His words "bring out your souls"? It is said: He said that to make it severe for them, like one who is expelled from a house against his will, and it is said to him, "Get out."

﴿Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth, and you were arrogant toward His signs.﴾ Al-hawn (al-hawn) is from humiliation (al-hawan), and al-hawn is from gentleness and kindness, as in His words: ﴿those who walk upon the earth in humility (hawnan)﴾.

"And you have indeed come to Us alone (furada), one by one, (wuhdanan fardan), ﴿just as We created you the first time﴾, without family or wealth, ﴿and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you⁠﻿ (mā khawwalnākum) behind your backs﴾. That is: We gave you possession (mallaknākum). Al-khawl means the slaves and servants (al-mamālīk).

﴿And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners among you﴾. He means by this what they claimed: that the idols and the angels are our intercessors with God.

﴿Indeed, all ties between you have been severed﴾: that is, what connected you (waṣalakum). It is like His words: ﴿and their ties were cut off from them⁠﻿ (wa-taqaṭṭaʿat bihim al-asbāb)﴾, meaning the means of connection (al-mawṣilāt). It is also read "laqad taqaṭṭaʿa baynakum" with a fatha on the nūn (tanwīn-less naṣb), and its meaning is: the matter has been cut off among you (taqaṭṭaʿa al-amru baynakum).

﴿And what you used to claim has strayed away from you.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 95:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah is the Splitter of the grain and the date-stone.﴾ Al-falq means al-shaqq (the splitting). Its meaning is that He splits the grain, so that the ear (of grain) is brought forth from the seed, and He splits the date-stone, so that the palm tree is brought forth from the stone. Included in His saying ﴿the Splitter of the grain﴾ are all seeds and grains, and included in His saying ﴿and the date-stone﴾ are the stones of all trees, such as the apricot stone, the peach stone, the stone of al-ghabira'(a kind of plum), and the like. It has also been said that "fāliq al-ḥabb wa al-nawā" means "khāliq al-ḥabb wa al-nawā" (the Creator of the grain and the date-stone).

﴿He brings forth the living from the dead and brings forth the dead from the living.﴾ We have already mentioned this and the difference of recitation regarding it, and the difference between "al-mayyit" and "al-mayyit" [as recited]. ﴿That is Allah; so how are you deluded?﴾ That is, how are you turned away?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 96:

God's words, ﴿Fāliq al-iṣbāḥ﴾ (the Splitter of the dawn), mean: He brings forth the morning light out of the night. Al-iṣbāḥ is a verbal noun (maṣdar), and here it carries the meaning of al-ṣubḥ (the dawn), so the sense is: Splitter of the dawn. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i read it as "faliq al-iṣbāḥ," and al-Hasan read it as "fālaq al-iṣbāḥ" with the qāf in the accusative. These two are shādh (irregular, non-canonical readings).

﴿And He made the night a resting-place﴾: that is, one rests in it. It is also read "wa-jaʿala al-layla sakanan," meaning: God made the night a resting-place. ﴿And the sun and the moon [He made] as a reckoning﴾: that is, according to exact calculation. Ḥusbān (reckoning) here means ḥisāb, in the sense that the two revolve by a known, measured reckoning. Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, who is a trustworthy transmitter from al-Nakha'i, reported from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that he said: It is permissible for a person to learn from the stars as much as is needed to know the stations of the moon and the courses of the stars, in order to determine the qibla and the times of prayer. ﴿That is the decree of the All-Mighty, the All-Knowing.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 97:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who made the stars for you, that you may be guided by them in the darkness of the land and the sea.﴾ This is one of the benefits of the stars. Allah, exalted is He, created the stars for several benefits. Among them is the adornment of the heaven, as the Exalted and Majestic said: ﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps.﴾ Among them is their use in pelting the devils, as He said: ﴿And We made them missiles against the devils.﴾ Among them is guidance in the darkness of the land and the sea, as He said here.

Abu al-Husayn Ibn Faris (Ibn Faris, a grammarian and lexicographer) related from some of the Successors (tabi'un) that by the stars here he meant the Companions, by whom one is guided in the darkness of polytheism. This is like his saying (ﷺ): "My Companions are like the stars; whichever of them you follow, you will be guided." ﴿We have made the signs clear for a people who know.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 98:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who produced you from a single soul﴾ means: Adam, peace be upon him. ﴿Then a place of settlement and a place of storage﴾. ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid said: by the place of settlement (mustaqarr) is meant the wombs of the mothers, and by the place of storage (mustawdaʿ) is meant the loins of the fathers. This is also related from Ibn ʿAbbās. It is also narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said, in the opposite way: the place of settlement is the loins of the fathers, and the place of storage is the wombs. ﴿And it is He who sent down water from the sky, and by it We brought forth the growth of every thing; then from it We brought forth green shoots, from which We bring forth grains piled up, and from the palm tree, from its spathe, clusters of dates hanging low, and gardens of grapes, and olives and pomegranates﴾, the mothers. It is related from Ibn Masʿūd that he said: the place of settlement is the wombs of the mothers, and the place of storage is the graves. There is also a third view: that the place of settlement is this world and the place of storage is the Hereafter. It is also read as "fa-mustaqirr" with a kasra on the qāf, and its meaning is: among you is one who settles, and among you is one who is stored. ﴿We have detailed the signs for a people who understand﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 99:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it is He who sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth by it the growth of every thing; then We bring forth from it green [shoots]﴾ — this is the tender branch — ﴿from which We bring forth grain piled up (mutarakiban)﴾, meaning piled one upon another. ﴿And from the palm trees, from their spathe, are clusters hanging low﴾. The ṭalʿ (spathe) is what emerges from the palm tree; the qinwān (clusters) are the ʿudhūq (strands of dates), whose singular is qinw. The ʿidhq (strand) is the base of the tree, and the ʿidhq is also the kubāsa (bunch), and ʿidhq and qinw are the same. The poet said:

(Dense like the cluster of the palm-tree, wrapped in its bunch...)

And he also said:

(Its upper parts have ripened, its roots have been crushed,
a cluster of unripe dates swaying with its red weight.)

As for "dāniyah" (hanging low), al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib said: ﴿qinwān dāniyah﴾ means near to the reach. In it there is an ellipsis, and its estimation is: clusters near and not near, i.e., near to the reach and far from the reach. One of them is omitted for brevity, since it comes to minds first. Similar to it is His saying: ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾, and its estimation is: protect you from the heat and the cold. His saying: ﴿and gardens of grapevines﴾ is read with the ta' pronounced with a kasra and with a damma. ﴿And the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar﴾, meaning similar, one resembling the other in leaf, and dissimilar in fruit and taste. And thus it is with the olive and the pomegranate: the leaf of the olive resembles the leaf of the pomegranate. It was said: its leaves extend down to the base of the tree like the leaves of the pomegranate, then it differs from the pomegranate in taste. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿similar and dissimilar﴾. ﴿Look at its fruit when it bears fruit and its ripening (yanʿihi)﴾, meaning its ripening. From this is the saying of al-Ḥajjāj when he gave a sermon and said: "I see heads that have ripened, and the time for their plucking has come, and I am, by God, their plucker," and he saw blood trickling between the beards and the turbans. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 6, verse 100:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they made the jinn partners with Allah﴾. This is because they used to say: the angels are the daughters of Allah, from the nobles (sarawat) of the jinn. ﴿And He created them﴾. It has been said: the pronoun refers back to the jinn. It has also been said: it refers back to the disbelievers, meaning: they say this, ﴿while He created them﴾. Yahya ibn Ya'mar read "wa-khalaqahum" (with the lam jazmed, i.e. "wa-khalqahum" with the final vowel dropped), and this is an anomalous (shadh) reading.

﴿And they attributed to Him sons and daughters without knowledge﴾. It is read with a light (takhfif) and with an intensive (tashdid) form. Al-kharq means fabrication, and al-takhriq means excessive fabrication from it. The meaning is: they fabricated for Him sons and daughters. This is like the saying of the Jews: "Uzayr is the son of Allah," and like the saying of the Christians: "The Messiah is the son of Allah," and like the saying of some of them: "The angels are the daughters of Allah." ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they describe.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 101:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning: the Innovator (mubdi') of the heavens and the earth. He is the Creator without any prior pattern. From this comes the word "innovators" (al-mubtadi'ah). A child can only come from a consort. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿How can He have a child when He has no consort and He created all things?﴾ It also indicates that He has no child, because when He created all things, nothing could be fit to be His child, since the created cannot be fit to be a child of the Creator. The offspring of everyone must be of his own kind. ﴿And He is Knowing of all things﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 102:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord; there is no god but Him, the Creator of all things﴾. He affirmed what had been mentioned before of the attributes of His oneness. ﴿So worship Him﴾, i.e., obey Him. ﴿And He is Guardian over all things﴾. It was said: He is the one who guarantees the provision (rizq) of creatures. It was also said: the wakil (Guardian) here means the one who sustains the creation of all things and manages them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 103:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision﴾. Those who hold the denial of the vision (ru'yah) have used this verse as evidence. They said: since He praised Himself by saying that no vision can grasp Him, His praise will be perpetual, in this world and in the Hereafter. Know that the vision of God is true according to the doctrine of the people of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah), and the Qur'an and the Sunnah have affirmed it.

God, exalted is He, said: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾. And He said: ﴿No indeed! They will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾.

And He said: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord﴾, and similar verses. Jarir ibn Abd Allah al-Bajali and others related with sound transmissions from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed you will see your Lord just as you see the moon on the night of the full moon, with no cloud between you and it, and you will not be wronged (la tudaymun) in seeing Him." And some narrate it as: "you will not be harmed (la tadarrun) in seeing Him."

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾, grasping (idrak) is other than seeing (ru'yah). Grasping is standing upon the essence and reality of a thing, whereas seeing is observing directly, and seeing may occur without grasping. God, exalted is He, said in the story of Musa: ﴿When the two hosts saw each other, the companions of Musa said, "We are surely overtaken." He said, "No indeed"﴾. Thus He negated grasping while affirming seeing. Since grasping is other than seeing, God, exalted is He, may be seen, but His essence is not grasped, since He has no essence that could be grasped. This is like the fact that He is known and recognized, yet He is not encompassed, as He said: ﴿and they do not encompass Him in knowledge﴾. Thus He negated encompassing while affirming knowledge. Ibn Abbas said, as transmitted by Muqatil from him, and the first view is the view of al-Zajjaj: the meaning of His saying ﴿No vision can grasp Him﴾ is: in this world. He sees creation, and creation does not see Him in this world, by the evidence of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾. Since the vision was affirmed by that verse for the Hereafter, it indicates that what is meant by this verse is grasping in this world, so that the two verses are reconciled. ﴿And He is the Subtle, the All-Aware﴾. Al-Latif: the one who delivers a thing with gentleness and kindness. It is said in supplication, "My Lord, be gentle with me (rabb ullutf bi)," meaning: deliver to me kindness. It was also said: its meaning is: He is gentle toward His allies and servants, and All-Aware of them.

"The Most High said: ﴿Indeed there has come to you insight (baṣā’ir) from your Lord.﴾ Baṣā’ir: the clear proofs (al-bayyināt). ﴿So whoever sees, it is for his own soul;﴾ meaning: his sight benefits him. ﴿And whoever is blind, it is against it;﴾ meaning: the harm of blindness falls upon it. ﴿And I am not a guardian over you.﴾ Meaning: I have not been commanded to keep you bound to me until you submit inevitably. It was said: this was at the beginning, and then it became abrogated (mansūkh) by the verse of the sword (āyat al-sayf)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 105:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We explain the verses﴾, meaning: We make the verses clear, one time in this way and another time in that way. ﴿And that they may say, "You have studied"﴾. It has been said: this is the "lam of consequence" (lam al-'aqibah), meaning: the outcome of their affair is that they will say, "You have studied." This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾. It is known that they did not pick him up for this purpose, but He intended that the outcome of his matter with them would be that he became an enemy to them; so this is called the lam of consequence. Likewise here.

As for His saying, ﴿درست﴾ (darasta, "you have studied"), it is read in several ways. "Darasta" means: you learned it from someone else, and they used to say that he had learned the reports of the earlier generations from Jabr and Yasar, who were two slaves of Byzantine (Rum) origin. It is also read "dārasta" (you have studied together/you have been in close study), meaning: you recited and drew near, and it derives from mudarasah (mutual study) between two people, one of whom studies with the other. Ibn 'Amir read "darasta," meaning: those are reports that have been effaced and erased. It is also read in the irregular (shadhdh) readings as "wa-liyaqulu darasta" with the meaning "erased," read by Qatadah. In the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud it is "wa-liyaqulu darasa," meaning: Muhammad has studied, and this means "learned," as we have explained. ﴿And that We may make it clear to a people who know﴾.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord, there is no deity except Him, and turn away from the polytheists.﴾ He means: the Qur'an.

God the Exalted says: ﴿And if God had willed, they would not have associated others with Him﴾, and this is evidence against the Qadariyya. ﴿And We did not make you a guardian over them﴾; we have already explained its meaning. ﴿Nor are you a manager over them﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 108:

His saying: ﴿And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah, lest they revile Allah in enmity without knowledge.﴾ It is also read, "ʿadwan bi-ghayri ʿilm" (ʿadwan, "in enmity"), and the two readings have one meaning, namely: transgression without knowledge. The occasion of revelation of the verse is that the disbelievers used to say to the Messenger of Allah: "Leave us and our gods, and we will leave you and your God" — and he used to mention their gods with evil. So the verse was revealed.

It is also related: "That some people from the disbelievers of Quraysh, from their chiefs, came to Abu Talib and said: 'Let your nephew leave us and our gods, and we will leave him and his god.' So the Messenger of Allah was called, and he said: 'Your people have come seeking fairness from you.' He said: 'And what do they want?' Abu Talib said: 'They say: Leave us and our gods, and we will leave you and your god.' The Messenger of Allah said: 'Will you give me one word? If you say it, the Arabs will submit to you, and the non-Arabs will pay you the jizya.' They said: 'And what is it?' He said: 'The word, there is no god but Allah.' So they recoiled and said: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a astonishing thing.﴾"

As for His saying: ﴿And do not revile those whom they call upon besides Allah﴾, although its apparent meaning is a prohibition against reviling the idols, its meaning is in fact a prohibition against reviling Allah, the Exalted, lest you revile their deities and so they revile Allah. This is like His saying (ﷺ): "None of you should curse his parents." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, and how would one curse his parents?" He said: "He curses another's father, so that person curses his father, and he curses his mother."

﴿Thus We have made attractive to every community their deeds.﴾ To the believers, their faith; and to the disbelievers, their disbelief. ﴿Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 109:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they swear by God their most solemn oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it.﴾ They were asking for signs and swearing that if they came, they would believe in them.

﴿Say: Signs are only with God.﴾ That is: the signs are in the hands of God, and God is able to send them down.

﴿And what will make you realise that when they come, they will not believe?﴾ His saying "annaha" (that it) is recited in two ways: with a kasra on the hamza and with a fatha on it. Whoever reads "innaha" (with kasra) takes it as a new beginning (ibtida', a fresh sentence). They differed about the meaning of His saying ﴿And what will make you realise﴾, and to whom it is addressed. Some of them said: it is addressed to the disbelievers, and its meaning is: "And what will make you realise, O disbelievers, that if they came, you would believe?" Then he begins: "Indeed, when they come, they will not believe."

It was also said: it is addressed to the believers, and its meaning is: "And what will make you know that if they came, they would believe in them?" For the believers were asking the Messenger of God to call upon God, exalted is He, so that He would show them a sign so that they might believe. So He said: "And what will make you realise that if they came, they would believe in them?" Then he begins and says: "Indeed, when they come, they will not believe." This refers to a specific people whom God knew would not believe.

As for whoever reads "annaha" with a fatha on the hamza, they differed about its meaning. Al-Kisa'i said: there is no extra particle here, and its implied sense is: "And what will make you realise that when they come, they will believe?" It was also said: "annaha" here means "la'allaha" (perhaps it), as the poet said:

(Show me a horse that has died of emaciation, for I
see what you see, or a miser who has lived forever.)

Its meaning is: "Perhaps I see what you see." Likewise here, its meaning is: "And what will make you realise? Perhaps when they come, they will not believe." It was also said: there is an ellipsis here, and its implied sense is: "And what will make you realise that when they come, they will believe or not believe?"

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And We turn their hearts and their eyes﴾, meaning: their hearts are turned so that they do not comprehend, and their eyes are turned so that they do not see; so they do not believe ﴿as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 111:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them﴾. The verse was revealed concerning what they demanded of signs. They had demanded all of this. They said, "We will not believe you until you send down to us a book from the sky carried by forty angels." They also asked for the revival of the dead, and they said, "Call upon God that He resurrect Qusayy, for he is a blessed elder, so that we may testify to you concerning prophethood." So the verse was revealed: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We had gathered against them every thing face to face﴾. Mujahid said: "Qubulan" is the plural of "qabil," and its meaning is: group after group. Others said: "qubulan" means in front of them, face to face. It is also read "qibalan" with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba', meaning: before their eyes. ﴿They would not have believed unless God willed, but most of them are ignorant﴾. In this verse there is clear evidence against the people of qadar.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 112:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy﴾, i.e., enemies. "Adu (enemy)" is a noun used for both the singular and the plural. ﴿Devils of mankind and of the jinn﴾. Al-A'mash recited: "shayatin al-jinn wa'l-ins" (devils of the jinn and of mankind). The shaytan (devil) is every rebellious, obstinate one, whether he is from mankind or from the jinn. It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Dhar: "Seek refuge with Allah from the devils of mankind." Abu Dhar said: "I said: And are there devils among mankind?" He (peace be upon him) said: "Yes," and recited this verse.

And it is related from Malik ibn Dinar that he said: "My fear of the devil of mankind is greater than my fear of the devil of the jinn, because the jinn departs when you remember Allah, whereas the human (insi) drags me to acts of disobedience."

﴿They inspire one another﴾, i.e., they cast to one another.

﴿Ornamented speech as deception﴾. Ornamented speech: it is a speech made attractive with nothing of substance beneath it; and ghurur (deception) is false speech. ﴿Had your Lord willed, they would not have done it﴾, i.e., the devils would not have cast whisperings into the hearts. ﴿So leave them and what they fabricate﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 113:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And so that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it﴾. This refers back to what preceded in His words: ﴿Thus We have made attractive to every nation its deeds﴾, and ﴿so that they incline to it﴾. The pronoun "it" (hu) is a reference to "embellished speech" (zukhruf al-qawl). That is, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter incline toward it. It was also said that the lam in it is the lam of consequence (lam al-'aqibah), as we have explained.

﴿And that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: That is, that they may know, from among the sins, what they were doing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 114:

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Shall I seek a judge other than Allah?﴾ Because they used to say to the Prophet: "Come, let there be a judge between us and you." He answered them with His words: "Shall I seek a judge other than Allah?!"

﴿It is He who has sent down to you the Book, fully detailed.﴾ That is: five by five and ten by ten. This is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "Why was the Qur'an not revealed to him all at once?" Thus [it is], that We may strengthen thereby your heart; and We have arranged it in gradual order.﴾ That is: We have made it detailed, so that We may strengthen your heart thereby.

﴿And those to whom We have given the Book﴾ That is: the Jews and the Christians, ﴿know that it is sent down from your Lord in truth.﴾ That is: the Qur'an. ﴿So do not be among the doubters.﴾

ِAnd the word of your Lord has been fulfilled, [in] truth and justice. ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled﴾ — by "the word" he means: His command and His prohibition, His promise and His threat, and the rulings and the signs. ﴿In truth and justice﴾ — truth in the promise and the threat, and justice in the command and the prohibition.

Qatadah said: "Truth in what He promised, and justice in what He decreed." ﴿None can alter His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 116:

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if you obey most of those on earth, they will mislead you from the way of Allah﴾. This is because most of the people of the earth were in misguidance. It was also said: He meant by it, "If you obey them in what they dispute concerning the permissibility of eating carrion and consuming it," ﴿they will mislead you from the way of Allah﴾, as will come later.

﴿They follow nothing but assumption, and they are only guessing﴾. That is: they are lying.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way﴾. It was said: this refers to Amr ibn Luhayy, and he was the first to alter the religion of Ibrahim (Abraham). ﴿And He is most knowing of those who are guided﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 118:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So eat of that over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs﴾. Meaning: eat of what has been slaughtered in the name of Allah.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran)** on Surah 6, verse 119:

﴿And why should you not eat of that over which the name of God has been mentioned?﴾ This was because the polytheists were disputing with the Muslims and saying: "You eat what you kill yourselves, but you do not eat what God has killed." They were inviting them to eat carrion (*maytah*) and to consider it lawful (*istihlal*). So these verses were revealed.

﴿And He has already explained to you what He has forbidden you.﴾ This is a detailed explanation of what has been enumerated among the prohibited things: carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, and what is similar to them in the Qur'an. ʿAṭiyyah recited "*wa-qad faṣṣala lakum*" (وَقد فصل لكم) with a light (*mukhaffafah*) pronunciation, meaning: it became manifest to you. It is like the reading in His words: ﴿whose verses have been made precise and then explained in detail﴾ with a light pronunciation. ﴿And He has already explained to you what He has forbidden you, except what you are compelled to; and indeed many lead others astray by their desires without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors.﴾

"The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And leave the outward and the inward of sin﴾. It is said: the outward of sin is fornication openly, and its inward is fornication secretly. The noble men of the Arabs used to refrain from fornication openly while committing it in secret. So the verse (is) concerning the prohibition of both of them together. Qatadah said: He intended by it the prohibition of all sins, secret and public. Apart from this, there are three opinions regarding the verse:

The first: that the outward of sin is marrying within the prohibited degrees (nikah al-mahārim), and its inward is fornication.

The second: that the outward of sin is uncovering the nakedness ('awrah), and its inward is fornication.

The third: that the outward of sin is that which the limbs commit, and its inward is that which the heart resolves upon, like one who persists in the sin and intends it.

﴿Indeed, those who earn sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit﴾. That is: the recompense for what they used to commit. And iqtiraf (ightiraf, "committing") is acquiring a sin (iktisab al-dhanb)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 121:

His statement ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: the verse concerns carrion (al-maytat) and what is similar to it, such as the strangled animal (al-munkhaniqah) and others. ʿAta' said: the verse concerns the slaughtered animals which they would slaughter in the name of the idols and not in the name of Allah, exalted is He.

There is a third view: that the verse concerns that over which the tasmiyah (invocation of the name of Allah) was omitted, as the apparent meaning requires. Then the scholars differed regarding that over which the tasmiyah was omitted. Al-Sha'bi and Ibn Sirin said: it is not lawful, whether the tasmiyah was omitted deliberately or forgetfully. ʿAta' and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: if the tasmiyah was omitted deliberately, it is not lawful; if it was omitted forgetfully, it is lawful. The first view is the view of Malik.

The sound view is that the verse concerns carrion, because He said: ﴿And indeed it is an act of transgression (fisq)﴾, and eating carrion is what constitutes transgression.

And He said: ﴿Indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you﴾, and their disputing was about eating carrion; for they would say: "You eat what you have killed yourselves, and you do not eat what Allah, exalted is He, has killed." So the verse was revealed.

﴿And if you obey them, indeed you are polytheists﴾, meaning: by deeming carrion lawful. Al-Zajjaj said: in this there is evidence that deeming the unlawful lawful, and making the lawful unlawful, entails disbelief (kufr).

In the reports: Ibn ʿAbbas was asked, and it was said to him: "Al-Mukhtar ibn Abi ʿUbayd claims that revelation comes to him." Ibn ʿAbbas said: "He speaks the truth, for Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Indeed, the devils inspire their allies﴾."

And in the report: the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There will emerge from Thaqif two men: a liar, and a destroyer who ruins." The liar is al-Mukhtar, and the destroyer is al-Hajjaj.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 122:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is one who was dead and We brought him to life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people⦆ Mujahid said: its meaning is: one who was astray and We guided him. ﴿And made for him a light by which he walks among the people﴾, that is, the light of Islam, by which he lives among the Muslims. ﴿Like one who is in darkness from which he will never emerge?﴾ Al-mithl (the like) here is redundant (sila), and its implied sense is: like one who is in the darkness, that is, in the darkness of polytheism, from which he never emerges at all. Al-Dahhak said: this was revealed concerning Umar and Abu Jahl. Ibn Abbas said: it was revealed concerning Ammar ibn Yasir and Abu Jahl. It was also said: it refers to Hamzah and Abu Jahl.

There is another opinion regarding the verse: that its meaning is: one who was dead through ignorance, and We brought him to life through knowledge. Every ignorant person is dead, and every knowing person is alive. The poet said:

(In ignorance, before death, there is a death for its people, and their bodies before the graves are graves.)

(Whoever has not been brought to life by knowledge is dead, and for him there is no resurrection before the Resurrection.)

﴿Thus was made attractive to the disbelievers what they used to do﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 123:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus We have placed in every town its greatest criminals﴾. Its meaning (taqdir) is: We have placed in every town its criminals as greatest ones (akabir). Its meaning is: just as We placed the criminals of Makkah as the greatest ones, so We placed in every town its criminals as the greatest ones. This is the sunnah (established way) of God in every town. Among His sunan (ways) is that He made their weak ones the followers of the Prophets, as He said in the story of Noah: ﴿And the lowest of the people follow you?﴾ It is narrated that Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, when he came to him, about the condition of the Prophet. Among what he asked him was: "Do his followers consist of the weak among them or of the noble (al-'ilyah)?" Abu Sufyan said: "Rather, the weak among them." Heraclius said: "They are the followers of the Prophets." There is a longer account in the report, and it is in the Sahih.

﴿That they may plot therein﴾. Among the plotting of the people of Makkah was that they placed four men at every road into Makkah, so that they would say to everyone who arrived: "Beware of this man, for he is a soothsayer, a sorcerer, a liar." ﴿But they plot only against themselves﴾, meaning: its harm returns upon them. ﴿And they do not perceive﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 124:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿When a sign comes to them, they say: "We will not believe until we are given the like of what was given to the messengers of God."﴾ That is: "We will not believe until revelation is sent down to us as it is sent down to him, and Gabriel descends upon us as he descends upon him." It is related that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira said: "If God intends to send a prophet, then I am more worthy of prophethood, for I have more wealth and am older in years." Their elders and leaders used to say the same, and so this verse was revealed.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿God knows best where to place His message.﴾ That is: God knows best who is fit for prophethood, and that Muhammad is fit for the message, while you are not fit for the message.

﴿Those who committed crimes will be struck with humiliation before God﴾. In this there are two meanings:

The first: al-Farra' said: its meaning is "humiliation from God," with "min" (from) omitted.

The Basrans said: "min" is not omitted, and its meaning is: humiliation that is established and lasting with God. ﴿And a severe punishment for what they used to scheme.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 125:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾.

That is: He opens his heart until Islam enters it. ﴿And whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast constricted and tight﴾.

It is also read "ḥarajan" (with a fatḥa on the rāʾ), meaning "one who has ḥaraj" (ḍayyiq, tight). As for with a kasra (ḥarijan), it is for emphasis in tightness. It is related from ʿUmar that he said: "I asked a Bedouin: What is the ḥarjah (thicket) among you?" He said: "A dense tree that neither a grazing animal nor a pasturing herd can reach." On this basis, the meaning of the verse is clear.

﴿He makes his breast constricted and tight﴾ such that faith cannot reach it and Islam cannot enter it. ﴿As if he were climbing up into the sky﴾. It is read in several ways: "yaṣʿadu" with two shaddas, meaning "yataṣaʿʿadu" (to make oneself climb), and it is likewise read in the irregular readings. It was also read "yuṣāʿidu" with a shadda on the ṣād, meaning "yataṣāʿadu," and "yaṣʿadu" with a light (unshaddated) ʿayn, from ṣuʿūd (ascent). All of these have one meaning.

Regarding its meaning there are two opinions. The first: its meaning is that it is as if he is charged with climbing and cannot manage it; the root of ṣuʿūd is hardship, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿I will overburden him with a arduous ascent (ṣaʿūdan)﴾, that is, a steep rising path. From this is the saying of ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him: "Nothing has been as burdensome (taṣaʿʿadanī) to me as the proposal of marriage," that is, nothing was as hard on me as the proposal of marriage.

The second opinion: the meaning of His saying, ﴿as if he were climbing up into the sky﴾, is a distancing from wisdom and a fleeing from the Qur'an.

(Thus Allah places the ruj's (filth) upon those who do not believe.) Ar-rijs (ar-rijs): it is the stench, and ar-rijz: the punishment. And in a report: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to say upon entering the privy: 'O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the impure, the evil, the vile filth of the accursed Satan.'" It was said: the curse in this world, and the punishment in the next.
His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And this is the path of your Lord, straight﴾, meaning: Islam. {﴿We have detailed the verses for a people who take heed﴾)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an, Qur'anic exegesis) on surah 6, verse 127:

﴿For them is the abode of peace with their Lord.﴾ *As-Salam* is Allah, the Exalted, and *Dar as-Salam* is Paradise. Al-Zajjaj said: He meant by *as-salam* the *salama* (safety), that is, for them is the abode of safety from calamities.

﴿And He is their Protector because of what they used to do.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 128:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them all﴾. As for the gathering of the jinn and mankind, it is a truth that must be believed in. ﴿O assembly of jinn, you have taken a great portion of mankind﴾, meaning: you have taken a great portion of mankind through seduction and misguidance. ﴿And their allies among mankind will say﴾, meaning: the disbelievers and the allies of the devils will say on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿Our Lord, we have enjoyed one another﴾, meaning: the jinn enjoyed mankind and mankind enjoyed the jinn. It has been said: the enjoyment of the jinn from mankind is their adorning [evil] for them and facilitating for them the path of error.

As for the enjoyment of mankind from the jinn, it is their obedience [to the jinn]. The summary is that the enjoyment of the jinn is through command, and the enjoyment of mankind is through acceptance. It has also been said: its meaning is that a man of the Arabs, whenever he descended into a valley, would say: "I seek refuge with the lord of this valley from the foolish ones of his people," and then he would spend the night safe from the jinn's harassment. This is the enjoyment of mankind from the jinn. As for the enjoyment of the jinn from mankind: that jinn whom the human sought refuge with would say to his people: "Mankind seek refuge with us; so we are the lords of the jinn and mankind." This is made clear in His saying, may He be exalted, in Surat al-Jinn: ﴿And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge with men from the jinn, so they increased them in burden﴾, meaning: in arrogance and pride.

﴿And we have reached our term which You appointed for us﴾, meaning: the term of the Resurrection.

﴿He will say: The Fire is your abode﴾, meaning: Allah says: The Fire is your abode, ﴿abiding therein eternally, except what Allah wills﴾. If someone says: Is it not the case that the disbelievers abide eternally in the Fire, all of them? Then what is this exception?

Answer: al-Farra' said: it is like His saying: ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, meaning: beyond the duration of the endurance of the heavens and the earth. This is also the intended meaning of this verse. It has also been said: the exception concerns the punishment, meaning: abiding in a kind of punishment, except what Allah wills of the other punishments.

It has also been said: it is an exception for the duration of the Resurrection and the reckoning, when they are not punished during the time of the Resurrection and the reckoning. ﴿Indeed your Lord is All-Wise, All-Knowing﴾.

Almighty God says: ﴿And thus We make some of the wrongdoers allies of one another﴾. He means: We cause them to follow one another in the Hereafter, into the Fire. It has also been said: this refers to the world, and its meaning is that We take vengeance on the wrongdoer through the wrongdoer, by giving some of them power over others. ﴿According to what they used to earn﴾, that is, as recompense for what they used to do.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 130:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O assembly of jinn and humankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you?﴾ If someone says: "Are there messengers from among the jinn, just as there are from among humankind?"

The answer: al-Dahhak said: "Yes, there are messengers from both species (al-thaqalan), as the Book has stated." Mujahid said: "The messengers are from humankind, and as for the jinn, among them are warners (nudhur), as God, exalted is He, said: ﴿and they returned to their people as warners﴾." According to this, the verse has two meanings. The first is that His saying ﴿messengers from among you﴾ refers to one of the two categories, namely humankind, and similar to it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿from both of them come forth pearls and coral﴾, where what is meant is one of the two seas, the salty and not the sweet.

The second is that the messengers are from both categories, except that the term "messengers" was used for the warners from among the jinn by way of meaning, since the warner has the sense of a messenger.

﴿They relate to you My verses and warn you of the meeting of this your day. They say: "We bear witness against ourselves."﴾ That is when their limbs speak. ﴿And the life of this world deceived them.﴾ This is from the speech of God, exalted is He, interjected in between. ﴿And they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.﴾

This is the commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 131:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿That is because your Lord would never destroy the cities unjustly while their people were unaware﴾. He means: that [sending of messengers and sending down of books] is so because Allah, exalted is He, does not destroy a town before sending a Messenger to it and warning it through revelation. This is because Allah, exalted is He, has established His practice that He does not seize anyone for a sin except after the sin has come into existence, and a person is only sinful when he is commanded and does not comply, is forbidden and does not refrain, and is called and does not respond.

Almighty Allah's saying: ﴿And for each there are degrees according to what they have done﴾ — that is, degrees in recompense according to what they have done. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware﴾ — that is, not heedless — ﴿of what they do.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 133:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And your Lord is the Self-Sufficient, the Possessor of mercy. If He wills, He can remove you and grant succession to whom He wills after you﴾. That is: if He wills, He can destroy you, and grant succession after you to whomever He wills. ﴿As He produced you from the descendants of another people﴾, by which He destroyed them and brought you into being after them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 134:

﴿Surely what you are promised is coming﴾, that is: every promise will come to pass. ﴿And you cannot escape it﴾, that is: you cannot get away from it.

(The words of Allah, the Exalted):) ﴿Say: O my people, act according to your standing.﴾ That is, according to your ability (tamakkun). It was also said: according to what you are upon. This is a command of threat, like His words: ﴿Act as you wish.﴾ Likewise His words: ﴿Act according to your standing; indeed, I am acting [likewise]. So you will come to know who will have the good outcome of the abode.﴾ That is, who will have the authority over the final outcome. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 136:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they assign to God a share of what He has created of the tilth and the cattle﴾. They used to divide the tilth, assigning a share to God and a share to the idols, and they would divide the cattle, assigning a share to God and a share to the idols. Then what they assigned to God, they spent on the poor and the needy, and what they assigned to the idols, they spent on the idols and on the servants of the idols. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿So they say, "This is for God," by their claim, and "This is for our partners."﴾ As for His saying: ﴿So what is for their partners does not reach God, and what is for God reaches their partners﴾, the meaning of this is: they, when they divided the tilth and the cattle as we have described, if some of what they had assigned to God from the tilth fell into what they had assigned to the idols, they left it; and if some of the share of the idols fell into what they had assigned to God, they returned it to the share of the idols. And if something from what they had assigned to God of the cattle perished or was diminished, they did not mind it; and if something perished or was diminished from the share of the idols, they made it up from what they had assigned to God, saying: God is independent, and the idol is in need. And when they suffered drought and famine, they would eat from what they had assigned to God, and would not eat from the share of the idols.

As for His saying: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾, that is: no revelation came to them concerning it, and reason does not require it; for analogy, according to their own claim, requires equality between the two partners, not what they judged.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 137:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And thus their partners have made attractive to many of the polytheists the killing of their children﴾. He means: just as this was made attractive to those people, so too it was made attractive to many of the polytheists, by their partners, the killing of their children through burying daughters alive, as we will explain. ﴿To ruin them﴾, meaning: to destroy them. ﴿And to confuse them regarding their religion﴾, meaning: to mix up their religion for them, since they were upon a remnant of the religion of Ibrahim (Abraham), so they confused their religion for them with what is not part of it. ﴿Had Allah willed, they would not have done it. So leave them and what they fabricate﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 138:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they say, "These are livestock and tilth, forbidden; none may eat of them except whom we wish," by their claim﴾ — meaning: forbidden. ﴿None may eat of them except whom we wish﴾ — then He explained their prohibition, saying: ﴿None may eat of them except whom we wish﴾, meaning: those who serve the idols. It was also said: it is the prohibition of the bahira and the saiba upon females, and none may eat of them except males.

﴿And livestock whose backs are forbidden﴾ — these are the hawami (protected animals) that we mentioned in al-Ma'idah; they used to say: "Their backs are forbidden." ﴿And livestock over which the name of Allah is not mentioned﴾ — it was said: these are slaughtered animals that they would slaughter in the name of the idols, not in the name of Allah, may He be exalted. It was also said that its meaning is: they do not ride them for a righteous deed. Abu Wa'il Shaqiq ibn Salamah said: its meaning is: they do not perform the Hajj upon them, nor ride them for the act of Hajj. However, it was the custom to mention the name of Allah upon righteous deeds, so He expressed the righteous deed by mentioning the name of Allah; thus He said: ﴿And livestock over which the name of Allah is not mentioned — a fabrication against Him﴾, meaning: a fabrication against Allah. ﴿He will repay them for what they used to fabricate﴾, meaning: a recompense for what they used to (lie about).

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And they say: What is in the wombs of these cattle is exclusively for our males﴾, meaning: the unborn young are lawful for our males. Al-A'mash read it as "khalis li-dhukurina" (خالص لذكورنا). Al-Kisa'i said: khalis and khalisah are one and the same, as one says wa'a'a maw'izah (وعظ موعظة), and there are similar examples. ﴿And forbidden to our wives﴾, that is, to our women. By this they meant what had been mentioned earlier concerning the offspring of the baheerah and the wasilah.

﴿But if it is dead﴾, meaning: if what is in the womb is stillborn, ﴿then they are all partners in it﴾, meaning the males and the females. It is also read "wa-in takun maytatan" (وَإِن تكن ميتَة). ﴿then they are all partners in it﴾. ﴿He will surely recompense them for their description﴾, that is, the recompense for their lying. ﴿Indeed He is Wise, Knowing﴾."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 140:

﴿Those who have lost are those who killed their children﴾ That is: they perished and were cheated, those who killed their children, and that was by burying daughters alive (wa'd al-banat). In the pre-Islamic era (al-Jahiliyyah) they used to bury girls alive, to the point that a man among them would kill his child and raise his dog. Some did this and others did not. It is said: this was practiced by two tribes, Rabi'ah and Mudar, who used to bury their daughters alive, whereas the Banu Kinanah and the rest of them did not do this.

﴿Foolishly, without knowledge﴾ That is: out of ignorance, not from insight. ﴿And they forbade what Allah had provided for them﴾ (namely) what we have mentioned of the prohibition of the offspring of the bahirah and the wasilah, and similar things, (and) the hawami, which they forbade out of religious devotion. ﴿Inventing a lie against Allah﴾ because they claimed it as a religion from Allah, the Exalted, and they lied about Him in that. ﴿They have certainly gone astray and were not guided.﴾

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 6, verse 141:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is He who produced gardens⁠﴾. "Gardens" (al-jannat): the orchards. ﴿Trellised and untrellised⁠﴾, meaning: some with trellises. The 'arsh (trellis) is the roof, and the vines are those with roofs. ﴿And untrellised⁠﴾: and among them is that which has no roof; likewise all other trees. ﴿And the date palm and crops, varying in their produce⁠﴾, meaning: their fruit.

﴿And the olive and the pomegranate, similar and dissimilar⁠﴾, meaning: similar in appearance, one resembling the other in its leaves, and dissimilar in fruit and taste. We have already explained this. It has also been said that it refers back to what was mentioned earlier of the vines, the date palms and the trees, for some of them resemble one another in leaves, fruit and taste, and some of them differ from one another.

﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit⁠﴾. This is a command of permission. ﴿And give its due on the day of its harvest⁠﴾, that is, the picking. It is also read "ḥaṣādihi" with a kasra on the ḥā'. It has been said that al-ḥaṣād and al-ḥiṣād are the same, like al-jazā' and al-jazā', and al-qaṭāf and al-qiṭāf. Then the scholars differed concerning what this due (ḥaqq) is. Ibn 'Umar and Abu al-Darda' said, (and this is the view of 'Ata' and Mujahid), that this due was a right in property besides the obligatory tithe (al-'ushr), and God commanded its payment.

Ibn 'Abbas and Anas said, (and this is the view of al-Hasan in one of the two narrations from him), that He meant by it the giving of the obligatory tithe (al-'ushr). From al-Hasan, in another narration, and this is the view of al-Nakha'i and Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that this was a due that they were commanded to give at the beginning of Islam, and then it became abrogated (mansukh) by the obligation of the tithe. The first view is preferable, because the verse is Meccan, and zakat was made obligatory afterwards in Medina; so interpreting it as a due other than zakat is preferable.

﴿And do not be wasteful⁠﴾, meaning: do not spend wealth in disobedience to God. Anyone who spends in disobedience is wasteful (musrif). It has also been said that it means giving away everything, such as when a man deliberately gives away all of his crops and palms and leaves his dependents destitute. It is narrated that Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas cut down five hundred palm trees that he owned and gave them all away, so the verse was revealed: ﴿And do not be wasteful; indeed, He does not love the wasteful⁠﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 142:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And of the livestock, some for carrying and some for slaughter (hamulatan wa farshan)﴾. That is: He produced from the livestock what is for carrying and what is for spreading out (farsh). Mujahid said: "The hamulah (carrying animals) are the large camels upon which loads are carried, and the farsh are the small ones." Al-Dahhak said: "The hamulah are the camels and the cattle, and the farsh are [the sheep]." The poet said:

(He bequeathed to me carrying animals and small ones... I wipe them down every day, morning and evening.)

That is: I wipe them down every day. ﴿Eat of what Allah has provided for you, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan﴾. That is: the traces of Satan and his misdeeds, and it is his stepping from the lawful to the unlawful. ﴿Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.﴾

ثَمَانِيَة أَزوَاج — The reason ثَمَانِيَة is in the accusative is that the word ﴿ثَمَانِيَة﴾ is a substitute (badal) for ﴿حمولة وفرشا﴾ (burden-bearing and carpet-like livestock). And the statement: ﴿ثَمَانِيَة أَزوَاج من الضَّأْن اثْنَيْنِ وَمن الْمعز اثْنَيْنِ﴾ and from the camels two and from the cattle two.

In reality these are four pairs (azwaj), each pair being two, because the Arabs call a single animal a zawj (mate) when it cannot be separated from its counterpart. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿وَمن كل شَيْء خلقنَا زَوْجَيْنِ﴾ "And of everything We created pairs."

﴿قل آلذكرين حرم أم الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ أما اشْتَمَلت عَلَيْهِ أَرْحَام الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ﴾ "Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain?" This refers to their prohibition of the Wasilah (a she-camel or ewe whose offspring was reckoned among their gods' portion) and the Bahirah (a she-camel whose ears were slit and whose milk was forbidden), and similar things. The verse is for the purpose of refuting them. The meaning is this: if the prohibition you attribute to Allah is because of maleness, then all males should be forbidden; if the prohibition is because of femaleness, then all females should be forbidden; and if it is because of what the wombs contain, then everything the wombs contain should be forbidden. So from where does the restriction of the prohibition to the seventh offspring or the fifth come? ﴿نبؤني بِعلم﴾ "Inform me with knowledge" — tell me with knowledge (إِن كَانَ لكم بِهِ علم) "if you have knowledge of it" ﴿إِن كُنْتُم صَادِقين﴾ "if you are truthful."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 144:

﴿And of the camels two, and of the cattle two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males or the two females, or that which the wombs of the two females contain?﴾ This is concerning their prohibition of the offspring of the baḥīrah (the she-camel whose ear was slit and set free) from the fifth belly, as has been mentioned earlier, and the basis of the argument against them is what we have explained.

﴿Or were you witnesses when Allah enjoined this upon you?﴾ Its meaning is: Did you say this on the basis of knowledge that you possess? Then inform me of it. {Or was it revealed to you by revelation? Or did Allah command you concerning it openly?}

﴿So who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah to mislead people without knowledge?﴾ Thus Allah makes clear, meaning: they are liars in this. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾

And in a report: "ʿAwf ibn Mālik al-Ashjaʿī came and said: 'O Muḥammad, you have made lawful what we have forbidden, and forbidden what we have made lawful—meaning the carrion.' So he recited these verses to him, and he recognized the proof and fell silent."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 145:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden﴾. The occasion of this was that they said: "Then what is forbidden?" So He revealed His saying: Say, O Muhammad: I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden ﴿to an eater who eats it, unless it be carrion, or blood poured forth, or the flesh of swine﴾.

The scholars differed regarding this. ʿĀʾishah and Ibn ʿAbbās held that the prohibition is confined to these things, and Mālik also held this view. They said: His saying ﴿unless it be carrion﴾ includes the strangled animal, the animal beaten to death, and what is enumerated in Sūrat al-Māʾidah. Mālik regards whatever is beyond these as disliked (makruh) but does not regard it as forbidden (ḥarām). The majority of scholars hold that the prohibition extends beyond these things; some of them were established by the Book (the Qur'an), and some by the Sunnah, and all of them are forbidden. It has been established that ﴿he (ﷺ) forbade every animal with fangs among the beasts of prey and every bird with talons﴾. ﴿For it is an abomination﴾, that is, foul-smelling; ﴿or a sin, that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked﴾, which is the animal slaughtered in the name of an idol. This is called a sin because it departs from the command of Allah, may He be exalted.

﴿But whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing, then indeed your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. We have already mentioned this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 146:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And to those who were Jews We forbade every animal with claws﴾. He means: We forbade the Jews every animal with claws. It has been said: this refers to the camel and the ostrich, and it also includes the goose and the duck.

﴿And of the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fat, except what their backs carry﴾. As for the prohibition of fat for them: it was concerning the thurb (the fat covering the intestines) and the fat of the two kidneys. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "May Allah curse the Jews. Fat was forbidden to them, so they melted it, sold it, and consumed its price."

His saying: ﴿except what their backs carry﴾ means: the fat of what their backs carry was not forbidden to them. ﴿Or the entrails﴾: its implied sense is "and the entrails," meaning the fat of the intestines. ﴿Or what is mixed with bone﴾: meaning and the fat of what is mixed with bone. It has been said: this is the rump fat (al-iliyah), and it has been said: it is the fat of the flank. Then they differed over whether all of these enter into the exception. Some of them said: only the fat of the backs enters into the exception, while ﴿or the entrails or what is mixed with bone﴾ returns to the prohibition. The correct view is that all of them enter into the exception, and this is the apparent meaning of the verse. ﴿That We repaid them for their rebellion﴾, meaning: [for their wrongdoing]. ﴿And indeed We are truthful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 147:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if they deny you, say: "Your Lord is the Lord of vast mercy."﴾ If it is said: What is the meaning of this, since the threat of punishment is more fitting for their denial than the promise of mercy? Tha'lab said: It is mercy by delaying the punishment from them, not by abandoning the punishment altogether. This is a good interpretation, based on His saying: ﴿And His punishment is not averted from the criminal people﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, when its time [comes]. Tha'lab was asked: Did not God, exalted is He, punish the disbelievers in this world? He said: This refers to the disbelievers among the people of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), whom God did not punish, by his blessing among them, just as He said: (﴿But God would not punish them while you are among them﴾, and We did not send you except as a mercy to the worlds).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 148:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The idolaters will say: "Had Allah willed, neither we nor our fathers would have associated anything with Him, nor would we have forbidden anything."﴾ Thus did those before them deny until they tasted Our might.﴾ The people of qadar (divine decree, i.e. those who deny the scope of divine decree in human action, the Qadariyya) used this verse as evidence, for when they said: "Had Allah willed, we would not have associated," Allah, exalted is He, refuted them and rejected their saying, saying: ﴿Thus did those before them deny.﴾ It has been said: the meaning of the verse is that they were speaking the truth, except that they were treating this (claim) as an excuse for themselves and making it an argument for themselves in abandoning faith. So the rebuttal against them was on this basis, by evidence.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 149:

His saying, exalted is He, after this: ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs the conclusive argument."﴾ That is: the argument through the command and the prohibition remains established for Him against them, even if He had willed that they not associate others with Him.

﴿Then if He had willed, He would have guided you all.﴾ If this is not understood in this sense, it would contradict the first statement. It was also said: they used to say, "Allah commanded us to associate others with Him," just as He said in al-A'raf: ﴿And when they commit an immorality, they say, "We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to it."﴾ And the sense of their saying, ﴿Had Allah willed, we would not have associated [others with Him]﴾ is: "He is the One who commanded us to associate others with Him." So the refutation here is directed at this claim, not at the occurrence of association by His will, for that is true and correct, and this is the view of the People of the Sunnah.

﴿Say: "Do you have any knowledge that you can produce for us?"﴾ That is: any book, so that you may produce it for us, until what you claim about Allah (that He commanded association) becomes clear. ﴿You follow nothing but conjecture﴾ meaning: you say what you say out of conjecture, not from insight. ﴿And you are not but guessing﴾ meaning: you are lying. ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs the conclusive argument; so if He had willed, He would have guided you all."﴾

Allah's saying, "Say: Bring forward your witnesses": that is, bring your witnesses ﴿who testify that Allah has forbidden this﴾. This refers back to what preceded, namely their forbidding things for themselves without any command from Allah, while claiming that it was from Allah's command.

﴿And if they testify, do not testify along with them﴾. That is: if they testify falsely, then do not testify along with them. ﴿And do not follow the desires of those who denied Our signs, and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and who set up equals with their Lord﴾. That is: who associate partners with Him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 151:

God's words, ﴿Say: "Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you: that you associate nothing with Him"﴾. They asked him, "What is it that God, exalted is He, has forbidden?" So God, exalted is He, sent down His words, ﴿Say: "Come, I will recite to you what your Lord has forbidden you"﴾. If someone says: God, exalted is He, did not forbid abandoning shirk; rather He commanded His servants to do so. So what is the meaning of His words, ﴿that you associate nothing with Him﴾?

There are two answers to this.

The first: His words "that not" (alla) are an extra particle (silah), and the sense is "that you associate." According to this, the statement is sound.

The second: His words ﴿"Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden"﴾ form a complete statement. Then His words ﴿"upon you: that you do not associate"﴾ begin a new statement. When it is construed in this way, the statement is also sound. Then His words ﴿and to parents, kindness﴾ mean: and show kindness to parents.

﴿And do not kill your children out of poverty﴾. Al-Mu'arrij said: al-imlaq (poverty) means hunger in the dialect of Himyar, while the well-known meaning in the language is poverty. ﴿We provide for you and for them﴾, meaning the provision of all of them is upon Us; so do not kill them for fear of hunger and poverty.

﴿And do not approach the indecencies, what is apparent of them and what is concealed﴾. This is a prohibition of all kinds of fornication, openly and secretly. In the Jahiliyyah, prostitutes were of two kinds: some of them had banners at their doors as a sign for whoever wished to commit fornication, and they would fornicate openly; others would fornicate secretly. Thus, the meaning of the indecencies here is "what is apparent of them and what is concealed."

﴿And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right﴾. He forbade killing by injustice and permitted killing by right, and this is explained in the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The blood of a Muslim man is not lawful except in one of three cases: disbelief after faith, or fornication after marriage, or killing a soul without a soul [i.e., in retaliation]." ﴿That He has enjoined upon you, that perhaps you will use your reason﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 152:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not approach the property of the orphan except in the way that is best﴾. The discussion of approaching the property of the orphan has already preceded in Surat al-Nisa'. ﴿Until he reaches his maturity (ashuddahu)﴾. Al-Suddi said: his ashudd is thirty years. Others said: it is the time of puberty (awan al-hulm). It was also said: it is the completion of strength, and its explanation will come in a later place.

﴿And give full measure and weight with justice﴾, that is, with fairness. ﴿We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity﴾, that is, its ability. ﴿And when you speak, be just, even if it concerns a near relative﴾, that is, be truthful, even if it is against a relative. ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah. This He has enjoined upon you, that you may remember﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 153:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And that this is My path, [which is] straight, so follow it﴾. It is read "wa-anna" with the shadda (tashdid), in which case it refers back to His saying: ﴿Recite what your Lord has forbidden you﴾, meaning: "And recite to you that this is My path." It is also read "wa-anna" with the shadda removed (takhfif), in which case it is a relative/linking element (silah), and its implied sense is: "This is My path, straight."

﴿So follow it and do not follow the [other] ways﴾, meaning: all the other creeds apart from the religion of Islam. It was also said: it refers to whims (ahwa') and innovations (bida').

﴿Lest they separate you from His way﴾, i.e., lest they separate you from His way.

﴿That He has enjoined upon you that you may be righteous﴾. It has been authentically related, through the narration of Ibn Mas'ud from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he drew a line, and drew lines around it, then pointed to the middle line and said: "And that this is My path, [which is] straight, so follow it." Then he pointed to the lines around it and said: "Do not follow the ways, lest they separate you from His way."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 154:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then We gave Musa the Book﴾. If it is said: how does He say ﴿Then We gave Musa the Book﴾ after mentioning Muhammad, when Musa was given the Book before him, and the particle "thumma" (then) indicates sequence? It is said: its meaning is: "Then I inform you that We gave Musa the Book."
