﴿Complete [blessing] upon the one who did good﴾. It is said: by "the one who did good" He means Musa, and the meaning is that, just as he did good in obeying his Lord and following His command, We completed upon him the blessing and the favour by giving him the Torah.

Al-Hasan said: its meaning is "complete [blessing] upon the good-doers of his people," and among them were both the good and the wrongdoer. This is the meaning of the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "Complete [blessing] upon those who did good." Yahya ibn Ya'mar read: "ʿalā alladhī aḥsana," with "aḥsana" in the raised (nominative) form (ḥasanun), meaning: "upon him who is the best (ahsan)."

﴿And an explanation of all things, and guidance and mercy﴾. This is in describing the Torah. ﴿That they may believe in the meeting with their Lord﴾.

"His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And this is a Book﴾, then He described the Qur'an: ﴿which We have sent down, blessed, so follow it﴾. We have already explained the meaning of "blessed" (mubarak). ﴿And fear Allah, that you may receive mercy﴾."

(أَن تَقولُوا) That is: lest you say, according to the view of the Kufans (i.e., "karahata an taqulu," "out of dislike that you should say"). As for the view of the Basrans, the implied phrase is: "an la taqulu" ("lest you should not say"): ﴿That the Book was sent down upon two groups before us﴾, meaning: the Jews and the Christians, ﴿and we were indeed unaware of their study﴾, that is: and we had indeed been ﴿heedless of their studying﴾. The meaning of the verse is: We have only sent down the Qur'an to you lest you say: "The Book was sent down to those before us in their language and tongue, so we did not understand what is in it, and we were heedless of studying it." Thus you would be creating an excuse for yourselves and a proof against Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 157:

﴿Or lest you should say: "Had the Book been revealed to us, we would surely have been better guided than they."﴾

Some of the disbelievers said this: "If what was revealed to the Jews and the Christians had been revealed to us, we would have been better than them and more rightly guided." Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Now there has come to you a clear proof from your Lord, and a guidance and a mercy﴾, meaning: the Qur'an has come to you; yet you denied it. Then He said: ﴿So who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of Allah and turns away from them?﴾, that is, turns away from them. ﴿We will repay those who turn away﴾, that is, who turn aside, ﴿from Our signs with a dreadful punishment because they used to turn away.﴾ His statement, exalted is He: ﴿[Do they await] …﴾, that is, after their denial of the Messengers and their rejection of the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 158:

﴿Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them?﴾ It has been said: with the punishment; and it has been said: with the taking of souls. (﴿Or your Lord should come﴾) meaning: on the Day of Resurrection, as He said in Surah al-Baqarah: ﴿Do they await anything but that Allah should come to them in canopies of cloud?﴾ and we have explained that there. ﴿Or some of the signs of your Lord should come﴾. The exegetes have agreed that it refers to the rising of the sun from its west, except in a single, anomalous report from Mu'adh ibn Jabal that it refers to the emergence of the Dajjal and the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj. It is established, through the report of Ibn Mas'ud from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said concerning it: "It is the rising of the sun from its west." Likewise Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated it as a marfu' report with the same wording.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Indeed the sun and the moon will rise on that day black." Safwan ibn 'Assal al-Muradi narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed, for repentance there is a door before the west, whose width is seventy cubits; it remains open until the sun rises from its west, and then it is closed, and repentance is not accepted after that." This is the meaning of the words of the Exalted: (﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, no soul will benefit from its faith﴾) — that is, a disbeliever's repentance by faith will not be accepted, nor will a sinner's repentance by turning away from sin. ﴿Say: Wait, indeed we are waiting.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 159:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, those who divided their religion and became sects, you have no connection with them in anything.﴾

Abu Umamah al-Bahili narrated, from Sada ibn Ajlan, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "They are the Kharijites." Mujahid said: They are the people of desires (ahl al-ahwa') and innovations (bid'a). It was also said: They are the people of all the other religions, the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, and others like them. And from Ibn Mas'ud, that he said: "The truest speech is the Book of Allah, the best guidance is the guidance of Muhammad, and the worst of matters are their innovations, and every innovation is a bid'a, and every bid'a is misguidance, and every misguidance is in the Fire." It is also narrated in this wording as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet, ﷺ) report. His saying, ﴿you have no connection with them in anything﴾ means: they are not of you, and you are not of them. ﴿Their affair rests with Allah; then He will inform them of what they used to do.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 160:

His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed, he will have ten times the like of it; and whoever comes with an evil deed, he will not be recompensed except with the like of it, and they will not be wronged.﴾ This is a favour from Allah, may He be exalted, in that He repays a good deed with ten times its like and an evil deed with its like. Ibn 'Umar said: This applies to good deeds other than charities (sadaqat). As for charities, they are multiplied by seven hundred times. Abu Salih said: The good deed is the statement "There is no god but Allah." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the statement "There is no god but Allah": is it among the good deeds? He said: "It is the best of the good deeds."

The Exalted said: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path, a upright religion﴾, which is the religion of Islam, meaning: a straight religion. ﴿The creed of Abraham﴾ is in the accusative on the basis of incitement (al-ighra'), meaning: follow the creed of Abraham. ﴿A man of pure faith (hanifan), and he was not of the polytheists﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 162:

﴿Say: Indeed, my prayer and my rites of sacrifice﴾. As for ṣalāh (prayer), it is well known; as for nusk, it is worship. It has also been said that by it he meant the sacrificial animal. And His saying: ﴿and my living and my dying are for Allah﴾, meaning: my obedience during my life is for Allah, and my recompense after my death is from Allah, {Lord of the worlds.
﴿He has no partner. I have been commanded to this, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾. He means: from this community.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 164:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things?﴾ This was because they (the disbelievers) would say to him: "Return to our religion, and if you fear Allah, we will take upon ourselves your punishment." This was said by the disbelievers of Quraysh, so it was revealed: ﴿Say: Shall I seek a lord other than Allah, while He is the Lord of all things?﴾ ﴿And no soul earns [sin] except against itself, and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another.﴾ That is: this is not a matter in which surety avails, and one cannot stand in the place of another regarding it. ﴿Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about that over which you used to differ.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 6, verse 165:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is He who has made you successors (khala'if) on the earth﴾, meaning: some of you succeed others. ﴿And He has raised some of you above others in degrees﴾, meaning: in this world, through poverty and wealth, sickness and health, and the like. ﴿That He may try you in what He has given you﴾, meaning: that He may test you regarding what He has bestowed upon you.

﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in retribution﴾, and everything that is coming is swift. ﴿And indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.
